The Second Discussion: concerning the readings (qira'at). It was read as ﴿shahadah﴾ (witness) without the taa' (feminine), because the witnesses (shuhada') are a group, or because they are in the sense of the selves (anfusuhum). As for the one who reads arba' (four) in the accusative: it is in the position of an infinitive (masdar) and the governing element is the masdar which is "fa-shahadatu ahadihim," and it is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is omitted; so its estimate is "fa-wajibu shahadati ahadihim arba'a shahadat" (then obligatory is the testimony of one of them: four testimonies). It was also read as "anna la'nata Allah" and "anna ghadaba Allah" with the lightening of anna and the raising of what follows it. It was read as "an ghadiba Allahu," with the verb of anger (ghadiba). And it was read with the fifth in the accusative, in the sense of "wa-yashhadu al-khamisata" (and he testifies the fifth).

* * *

The Third Discussion: concerning the rulings, and the consideration of it relates to several parts.

The First Part: concerning what makes li'an binding, and it contains issues.

The first issue: Know that when a man accuses his wife of adultery, it is obligatory upon him the hadd if she is muhsanah (chaste/married), and the ta'zir (discretionary punishment) if she is not muhsanah, just as in accusing an unrelated woman, their consequence does not differ, except that they differ in the means of release. In slandering an unrelated person, the hadd does not fall from the slanderer except by the confession of the one slandered, or by evidence that establishes her adultery. In slandering a wife, the hadd falls from him by one of these two matters or by li'an. The Law only took li'an into account in this case and not with unrelated women for two reasons:

The first: there is no shame upon him in the adultery of an unrelated woman, and it is better for him to conceal it. But if he commits adultery with his wife, shame and a corrupt lineage fall upon him, so he cannot bear it, nor can he be held to the proof like one who apologizes. Therefore the Law specifically assigned this case to li'an.

The second: in the customary circumstances of a man with his wife, he generally does not intend to slander her except out of certainty; so when he accuses her, the accusation itself testifies to his truthfulness. However, the testimony of circumstance is not complete, so there is added to it what strengthens it of oaths, like the testimony of a woman: when it was weak, it was strengthened by increasing the number. A single witness is strengthened by an oath according to the opinion of many jurists.

The second issue: Abu Bakr al-Razi said: The hadd for slandering unrelated women and wives was flogging. The evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to Hilal ibn Umayyah when he slandered his wife with Sharik ibn Sahma': "Bring four who testify for you, or else a hadd upon your back." Thus it is established by this that the hadd for slandering wives was like the hadd for slandering unrelated women, except that flogging was abrogated (naskh) for spouses by li'an. A similar narration was related about the man who said: "What do you think, if a man found a man with his wife, if he speaks you flog him, if he kills you kill him, and if he remains silent he remains silent in rage." So these reports indicate that the hadd for slandering a wife was flogging, and that Allah abrogated it by li'an.

The third issue: al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: If a husband slanders his wife, then what is obligatory is the hadd, but the way of release from it is li'an, just as what is obligatory for slandering an unrelated woman is the hadd, and the way of release from it is witnesses. So if the husband refuses li'an, the hadd for slander binds him. If he performs li'an and the wife refuses li'an, the hadd for adultery binds her. Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: If the husband refuses li'an, he is imprisoned until he performs li'an; and likewise, if the wife refuses, she is imprisoned until she performs li'an. The proofs of al-Shafi'i are several:

The first: Allah, exalted is He, said at the beginning of the surah: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾ meaning other than wives, ﴿then do not produce four witnesses, flog them eighty lashes﴾. Then He joined to it the ruling on spouses, saying: ﴿And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves, then the testimony of one of them﴾ up to the verse. So just as the requirement for slandering unrelated women is to produce witnesses or be flogged, likewise the requirement for slandering wives is to produce li'an or the hadd.

The second: the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And it will avert the punishment from her﴾ "that she testify four testimonies by Allah." The alif and lam attached to "al-'adhab" (the punishment) do not indicate generality, because not all kinds of punishment became obligatory upon her, so they must be directed to the previously known referent (al-ma'hud al-sabiq). The previously known referent is the hadd, because He, exalted is He, mentioned at the beginning of the surah: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, and what is meant by it is the hadd. And when it is established that what is meant by "the punishment" in His saying ﴿it will avert the punishment from her﴾ is the hadd, it is established that if she does not perform li'an she would be flogged, and that by li'an she averts the hadd. If it is said: what is meant by the punishment is imprisonment. We say: We have already shown that the alif and lam are for the previously mentioned referent, and the nearest of what has been mentioned in this surah is "al-'adhab" in the sense of the hadd. Also, if we take it to mean the hadd, the verse does not become ambiguous; but if we take it to mean imprisonment, the verse becomes ambiguous, because the amount of imprisonment is not known.

The third: al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Among what indicates the invalidity of imprisonment with regard to the woman is that she says: "If the man is truthful, then flog me; and if he is a liar, then release me. What is my case with imprisonment? My imprisonment is not in the Book of Allah, nor in the Sunnah of His Messenger, nor in consensus (ijma'), nor in analogy (qiyas)."

The fourth: the husband slandered her, and did not bring a way out through the testimony of another or the testimony of himself; so the hadd became obligatory upon him, by His saying: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women, then do not produce four witnesses, flog them﴾. And if this is established regarding the man, it is established regarding the woman, because there is no one who makes a distinction.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 24, verses 6–10 (part 2 of 3)**

And the fifth: his saying, peace be upon him, to Khawla: "Then stoning is easier for you than the wrath of Allah." This is a text on the matter, and it is the proof of Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him. As for the woman's case, she did nothing except refrain from li'an (the mutual oath of cursing between spouses). This refraining is neither clear evidence of adultery nor an admission by her of it. Therefore it is not permissible to stone her, based on his saying, peace be upon him: "The blood of a man is not lawful…" the hadith. And if stoning is not required when she is muhsana (a married woman who is protected by a valid marriage), then flogging is not required for one who is not muhsana, because no one holds a distinction. Also, nukul (refusal to take the oath) is not explicit in admitting the charge, so the hadd (prescribed punishment) may not be established by it, like an ambiguous word that could mean adultery or something else.

**The fourth issue:** The majority said that if he says to her, "O adulteress," li'an becomes obligatory. Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said that he does not perform li'an unless he says, "I saw you committing adultery," or he denies a pregnancy she carries or a child from her. The majority's proof is that the generality of His saying, ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾, encompasses everyone. Also, there is no difference in accusing a non-related woman among all people, so likewise in the case of accusing a wife.

* * *

**The second part: the one who performs li'an.** Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Whoever's oath (yamin) is valid, his li'an is valid. Thus li'an takes place between two slaves, two dhimmis (non-Muslim subjects under Muslim protection), and two people who have been subjected to hadd. Likewise if one of them is a slave, or if the husband is Muslim and the wife is a dhimmi. Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said that it is not valid in two cases. The first: that the wife is one for whom the hadd is not required upon her accuser if he were a stranger, such as when the wife is a slave or a dhimmi.

The second: that one of them is not among the people of testimony (shahada), such as one who has been subjected to hadd for qadhf (false accusation of unchastity), or a slave, or a disbeliever. Then he claimed that a fasiq (one who is openly sinful) and a blind man, even though neither of them is among the people of testimony, may perform li'an validly. The basis of al-Shafi'i's view, may Allah have mercy on him, is that the apparent meaning of His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ encompasses all, and there is no meaning to restricting it. Analogy (qiyas) is also apparent in two respects:

The first: the purpose is to ward off shame from oneself, and to ward off the child of adultery from oneself. Just as a non-hadd person needs this, so too a hadd person needs it.

The second: we are agreed that li'an is valid for a fasiq and a blind man, even though neither of them is among the people of testimony. Likewise the matter is for others. The common element (jami') is the need to ward off the shame of adultery.

The view of Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, rests on text and meaning. As for the text, what 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As related: that he, peace be upon him, said: "Four kinds of women have no li'an between them and their husbands: a Jewish woman and a Christian woman under a Muslim, a free woman under a slave, and a slave woman under a free man."

As for the meaning, we say: in the first case, the obligation upon one who accuses a wife or a stranger was the hadd, by His saying: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾. Then this was abrogated (naskh) for husbands, and li'an was put in its place. So when li'an with husbands stands in place of the hadd for strangers' accusations, li'an is not obligatory upon one on whom the hadd would not be obligatory if a stranger accused her. As for the second case, the view is that li'an is a testimony (shahada), so it must not be valid except from people of testimony. We said that li'an is a testimony for two reasons:

The first: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And they have no witnesses except themselves, so the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah﴾. So Allah named their li'an a testimony, as He said: ﴿And call upon two witnesses from your men﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282], and He said: ﴿Call upon four witnesses from among you against them﴾ [al-Nisa': 15].

The second: when he, peace be upon him, performed li'an between the spouses, he commanded them to perform it with the wording of testimony (shahada), and did not restrict it to the wording of oath (yamin). If it is established that li'an is a testimony, then it must be that the testimony of one subjected to hadd for qadhf is not accepted, based on His saying: ﴿And do not accept their testimony ever﴾ [al-Nur: 4]. And if this is established for one subjected to hadd, it is established for a slave and a disbeliever too, either by consensus that they are not among the people of testimony, or because no one holds a distinction.

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, replied that li'an is not testimony in reality; rather it is an oath, because a person may not testify for himself. Also, if it were testimony, the woman would have to bring eight testimonies, because she is half of a man in this regard. Also, it is valid from a blind man and a fasiq, yet their testimony is not accepted. If it is said that a fasiq and a fasiqa may repent, we say: likewise a slave may be freed, and then his testimony is accepted. Then al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, emphasized: when a slave is freed, his testimony is accepted immediately, whereas when a fasiq repents, his testimony is not accepted immediately. Then he held Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, to the argument that the testimony of dhimmis is accepted against one another, so li'an between a dhimmi man and a dhimmi woman should be valid. This is all the words of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him.

He then said after that: hudud (prescribed punishments) differ according to the person to whom they apply. The meaning is that if the husband does not perform li'an, the hadd for qadhf is halved for him because of his slavery. If he performs li'an and she does not perform li'an, her hadd differs according to her ihsan (chastity/protected status), her lack of ihsan, her freedom, and her slavery.

* * *

**The third part: the rulings that follow from li'an.** Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: five rulings are connected to li'an: the averting of the hadd, the negation of the child's paternity, separation (furqa), permanent prohibition (tahrim mu'abbad), and the obligation of the hadd upon her. All of these are established by his li'an alone, and it does not depend on her li'an or on a ruling of a judge (hakim). For the ruling of the judge concerning it is an execution (tanfidh) from him, not the initiation of separation. So let us discuss these issues:

**The first issue:** The mujtahids (qualified jurists) differed on whether separation occurs through li'an, in four views:

First: 'Uthman al-Batti said: I do not see that the husband's li'an with his wife requires anything that would obligate him to divorce her.

Second: Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said: separation does not occur upon their finishing li'an until the judge separates them.

Third: Malik, al-Layth and Zufar, may Allah have mercy on them, said: when they finish li'an, separation occurs even if the judge does not separate them.

Fourth: al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: when the husband completes the testimony and the li'an, his wife's bed (firash) is removed, and she is never lawful to him again, whether she performs li'an or not.

The proofs of 'Uthman al-Batti are several:

The first: li'an is neither explicit nor allusive (kinaya) regarding separation. Therefore it must not produce separation, like the other statements that have no indication of separation. For at most, it means that the husband is truthful in his statement, and that does not require prohibition. Do you not see that if evidence were established against her, that would not require prohibition? So if he is lying and she is truthful, it is established that there is no indication in it of prohibition.

The second: if they performed li'an between themselves, it would not require separation; likewise if they performed li'an before the judge.

The third: li'an stands in place of witnesses in the accusation of strangers. Just as there is no benefit in bringing witnesses there except to drop the hadd, likewise li'an has no effect except to drop the hadd.

The fourth: if the husband retracts his accusation of her and is then subjected to hadd, that does not require separation. Likewise if he performs li'an, because li'an stands in place of averting the hadd.

He said: As for the Prophet's ﷺ separation between the two who performed li'an, that was in the case of al-'Ajlani, and he had divorced her three times after the li'an, so for that reason he separated them. As for the view of Abu Hanifa, which is that the judge separates them, two matters must be explained:

One: it is obligatory upon the judge to separate them. Its proof is what Sahl ibn Sa'd related in the case of al-'Ajlani: "The sunnah has passed concerning the two who performed li'an, that they be separated and never come together again."

The second: separation does not occur except by the judgment of the judge. They argued for this with several points:

The first: it was narrated in the case of 'Uwaymir that when they finished, "'Uwaymir said: 'I have lied against her, O Messenger of Allah, if I keep her; she is divorced three times,' and he divorced her three times before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him." The argument from this report is in several respects:

The first: if separation had occurred through li'an, his saying "I have lied against her if I keep her" would be void, because keeping her would be impossible.

The second: what is narrated in this report, that he divorced her three divorces, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ executed it. The execution of divorce is only possible if separation had not occurred by the li'an itself.

The third: what Sahl ibn Sa'd said in this report: "The sunnah has passed concerning the two who performed li'an, that they be separated and never come together again." If separation had occurred by li'an, separating them afterward would be impossible.

The second: Abu Bakr al-Razi said: al-Shafi'i's view opposes the verse, because if separation occurred by the husband's li'an, the woman would perform li'an even though she is a stranger, and that opposes the verse, because Allah only obligated li'an between spouses.

The third: li'an is a testimony, whose ruling is not established except before a judge. Therefore it must not produce separation except by the judgment of a judge, just as what is testified to is not established except by the judgment of a judge.

The fourth: through li'an the woman acquires her own right, just as the claimant acquires his claim by evidence. Since the claimant may not acquire his claim except by the judgment of a judge, the same must apply to the woman acquiring her right.

The fifth: li'an has no indication of prohibition, because at most it states that she committed adultery. If evidence were established of her adultery, or she confessed to it, that would not require prohibition. Likewise li'an. When there is no indication in it of prohibition, separation must not occur by it. So separation must be brought about, either by the husband or by the judge.

As for the view of Malik and Zufar, their proof is that if the two agreed to remain married, they would not be left together but would be separated. This shows that li'an has obligated separation.

As for al-Shafi'i's view, may Allah have mercy on him, he has two proofs:

The first: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And she averts the punishment from herself by testifying﴾ and so on. This shows that the wife's li'an has no effect except in averting punishment from herself, and that all rulings obligated by li'an have occurred by the husband's li'an.

The second: the husband's li'an alone is independently sufficient to negate the child's paternity. Therefore the consideration must be his statement regarding attributing the child, not her statement. Do you not see that in her li'an she attributes the child to him, while we negate it from him? So the husband's negation is considered, not the wife's attribution. This is why, if the husband retracts his accusation, the child is attributed to him; and as long as he persists in li'an, the child is negated from him. Since it is established that his li'an is independently sufficient to negate the child, it must be independently sufficient for the occurrence of separation. For if separation did not occur, the child would not be negated, given His saying, peace be upon him: "The child belongs to the bed (firash)." As long as the bed remains, the child is attributed to it. So when the child is negated from him by his li'an alone, it must be that the bed is removed from him by his li'an alone.

As for the reports which Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, used as evidence, they mean that the Prophet, peace be upon him, informed of the occurrence of separation and ruled by it, and that does not preclude that the cause of separation was something else.

As for the analogies he mentioned, they rest on the premise that li'an is testimony, and the matter is not so; rather it is an oath, as we have explained. As for his statement that li'an has no indication of the occurrence of prohibition, we say: its evidence is in negating the child, which is accepted, and negating the child implies negating the lawfulness of marriage. And Allah knows best.

**The second issue:** Malik, al-Shafi'i, Abu Yusuf, al-Thawri, Ishaq and al-Hasan said: the two who performed li'an may never come together again. This is also the view of 'Ali, 'Umar and Ibn Mas'ud. Abu Hanifa and Muhammad said: if he retracts his accusation and is subjected to the hadd, the prohibition of the contract ceases, and she becomes lawful to him through a new marriage. The proofs of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, are several matters:

[p. 149]

First: the Prophet's ﷺ saying to the one who performed li'an (mutual oaths of condemnation), after the li'an was completed, "You have no claim over her" (ﷺ), without adding "until you retract your accusation." Had retraction been the condition for ending this prohibition, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have restricted it to that condition, just as he said regarding the woman divorced three times: ﴿So if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾ [al-Baqarah: 230].

Second: what is narrated from 'Ali, 'Umar and Ibn Mas'ud, that they said, "The two who have performed li'an never reunite, ever." This has also been narrated as a marfu' report traced to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Third: what al-Zuhri narrated from Sahl ibn Sa'd concerning the story of al-'Ajlani: "The sunnah has passed that when the two perform li'an, they are separated, and then they never reunite, ever." This is the proof of Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him), along with the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And lawful to you is what is beyond that﴾ and His words: ﴿So marry what is good for you﴾.

Third issue: The scholars agree that a child may be disowned from the husband through li'an. It is reported from some deviant individuals that the child belongs to the husband and that his lineage is not severed by li'an, and they cited the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "The child belongs to the bed." This view is weak, because the reports indicating that lineage is severed by li'an are like the mutawatir (widely transmitted) reports, so this single report cannot oppose them.

Fourth issue: al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: if one of the two spouses utters only some of the words of li'an, the ruling does not apply to them. Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him) said: most of the words of li'an act as the whole when the judge rules by it. The stronger view is that of al-Shafi'i, because it indicates that the woman cannot avert the punishment from herself except by completing what Allah the Exalted mentioned. Whoever holds otherwise does so on the basis of a separate proof.

* * *

Fifth section: On the manner of li'an. The verse explicitly indicates it. The man testifies four times by Allah, saying: "I testify by Allah that I am truthful regarding what I have accused her of, namely adultery." Then he says: "And the curse of Allah be upon me if I am among the liars." According to al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him), five rulings are connected to the husband's li'an. If the woman wishes to avert the punishment for adultery from herself, she must perform li'an, and only this one ruling is connected to her li'an. Here are some branches:

First branch: They agree that li'an is like testimony, so it is not established except before a judge.

Second branch: al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: the man is made to stand while he testifies, and the woman remains seated; the woman is made to stand while she testifies, and the man remains seated. The imam orders someone to place his hand over the man's mouth when he reaches the words about the curse and wrath, and says to him: "I fear that if you are not truthful, you will incur the curse of Allah."

Third branch: li'an may be performed in Mecca between al-Maqam and al-Rukn; in Medina, at the minbar; in Jerusalem, in its mosque; and elsewhere in the honored places. The li'an of a polytheist is the same as that of others in its manner. As for the time, it is Friday after the 'asr prayer. A group of notable persons must be present, the least of whom are four.

* * *

Sixth section: On the remaining benefits, and it contains issues.

First issue: Our companions (the Shafi'is/Ash'aris) used this verse to refute the view of the Khawarij (the Kharijites), that adultery and false accusation of adultery are kufr (disbelief), on two grounds:

First: If the accuser is truthful, she is an adulteress; if he is lying, he is a slanderer. So according to their view, disbelief must occur from one of the two. That would be apostasy, and it would follow that separation occurs and there is no li'an at all, and that it would be a separation by apostasy, so that no inheritance could ever be connected to it.

Second: If disbelief were established against her through his li'an, then she would have to be killed, not flogged or stoned, because the punishment of an apostate is distinct from the hadd (prescribed punishment) for adultery.

Second issue: The verse indicates the falsity of the view of one who says that the occurrence of adultery invalidates the marriage. This is because, if he accuses her of adultery, his statement must be as if he acknowledges the invalidity of the marriage, so that his position would be like that of one who acknowledges that she is his foster sister or that she is a disbeliever. If it were so, separation would have to occur by the mere accusation before li'an, and the invalidity of that has been established by consensus.

[p. 150]

Third issue: The Mu'tazila said: the verse indicates that the slanderer deserves the curse of Allah the Exalted if he is lying, and that he has committed fisq (grave sin). Likewise, the adulterer and the adulteress deserve the wrath and punishment of Allah the Exalted; otherwise it would not be proper for them to curse themselves, just as it is not permissible for anyone to ask his Lord to curse children and the insane. If that is valid, then he has deserved punishment, and punishment is permanent like reward, and they cannot coexist, so their reward is also nullified. Therefore, if they do not repent, it is not permissible for them to enter Paradise, because the community agrees that whoever among the obligated enters Paradise is rewarded for his acts of obedience, and that indicates the eternal abiding of the sinners in the Fire. Our companions said: we do not concede that being under wrath because of his sin contradicts being pleased with him for the sake of his faith. Even if we concede that, we do not concede that only one who deserves reward enters Paradise. And the consensus is disputed.

Fourth issue: The woman performing li'an was singled out to be subjected to five oaths with the wrath of Allah, as a heightening of severity upon her, because she is the root of immorality and its source, through her vanity and her desires. For this reason she is mentioned first in the verse about flogging.

Know that when He, glorified is He, explained the ruling for one who accuses chaste women and married women as we have mentioned, and there was in that a mercy and a blessing that is not hidden, because He, the Exalted, made through li'an a way for the man to reach his aim, and a way for her to avert the punishment from herself, and for both of them a way to repentance and turning back, then for this reason He, the Exalted, explained by His words: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾ [al-Nur: 14] the magnitude of His blessings in what He explained of these rulings, and in what He granted respite and preserved, and enabled for repentance. There is no doubt that there is an ellipsis in the speech, since an answer must exist; however, omitting it indicates that it is a great matter that cannot be fathomed, and many an unspoken matter is more eloquent than a spoken one.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 24, verses 6–10 (part 1 of 3):**

The Fourth Ruling: the ruling on li'an (mutual imprecation between spouses). His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves, then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the truthful. And the fifth (testimony) is that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars. And it will avert the punishment from her that she testify four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars. And the fifth (testimony) is that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful. And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Oft-Returning, All-Wise.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned the rulings on slandering unrelated women (qadhf al-ajnabiyyat), He followed it with the rulings on slandering wives. This verse contains several discussions.

The First Discussion: concerning the occasion of its revelation, and they mention several accounts about it.

The first: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah have mercy on both of them, said: "When the saying of Allah, exalted is He, ﴿And those who accuse chaste women, then do not produce four witnesses﴾ was revealed, 'Asim ibn 'Adi al-Ansari said: 'If a man among us enters his house and finds a man on the belly of his wife, if he brings four men who testify to that, then the man has accomplished his need and left. And if he kills him, he is killed for it. And if he says, I found so-and-so with that woman, he is flogged. And if he remains silent, he remains silent in rage.' O Allah, make it clear." 'Asim had a paternal cousin called 'Uwaymir, and he had a wife called Khawlah bint Qays. 'Uwaymir came to 'Asim and said: "I have seen Sharik ibn Sahma' on the belly of my wife Khawlah." So 'Asim said, "Inna lillah" (we belong to Allah), and went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, how quickly I have been tested with this in my household!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "And what is that?" He said: "My paternal cousin 'Uwaymir informed me that he saw Sharik ibn Sahma' on the belly of his wife Khawlah." 'Uwaymir, Khawlah and Sharik were all paternal cousins of 'Asim. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned all of them and said to 'Uwaymir: "Fear Allah concerning your wife and your paternal cousin, and do not slander her." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I swear by Allah that I saw Sharik on her belly,

[Page 144]

and that I have not approached her for four months, and that she is pregnant by someone other than me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "Fear Allah, and do not inform except of what you did." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, 'Uwaymir is a jealous man, and he saw Sharik looking at me for a long time and talking to me, so jealousy drove him to what he said." Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that it be announced: "Al-salah jami'ah" (prayer is gathering), and he prayed the 'Asr prayer. Then he said to 'Uwaymir: "Stand up and say: I bear witness by Allah that Khawlah is an adulteress, and that I am surely of the truthful." Then he said to him the second time: "Say: I bear witness by Allah that I saw Sharik on her belly, and that I am surely of the truthful." Then he said the third time: "Say: I bear witness by Allah that she is pregnant by someone other than me, and that I am surely of the truthful." Then he said the fourth time: "Say: I bear witness by Allah that she is an adulteress, and that I have not approached her for four months, and that I am surely of the truthful." Then he said the fifth time: "Say: May the curse of Allah be upon 'Uwaymir," meaning himself, "if he is of the liars concerning what he said." Then he said: "Sit down." And he said to Khawlah: "Stand up." She stood and said: "I bear witness by Allah that I am not an adulteress, and that my husband 'Uwaymir is surely of the liars." She said the second time: "I bear witness by Allah that he did not see Sharik on my belly, and that he is surely of the liars." She said the third time: "I bear witness by Allah that I am pregnant by him, and that he is surely of the liars." She said the fourth time: "I bear witness by Allah that he never saw me in an indecent act, and that he is surely of the liars." She said the fifth time: "The wrath of Allah be upon Khawlah if 'Uwaymir is of the truthful in his saying." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated the two of them."

The second: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, in the narration of al-Kalbi: "That 'Asim one day returned to his family and found Sharik ibn Sahma' on the belly of his wife, so he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ..." and the rest of the hadith is as mentioned before.

The third: what 'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "When the saying ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾ was revealed, Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, who was the chief of the Ansar, said: 'If I found a man on her belly, and I brought four witnesses, he would have finished his need and gone.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'O assembly of the Ansar, do you not hear what your chief says?' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, do not blame him, for he is a jealous man.' Sa'd said: 'O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I know that it is from Allah and that it is true, but I was surprised at it.' He, peace be upon him, said: 'Indeed Allah refuses except that.'" He said: "They had not waited long before a paternal cousin of his came, called Hilal ibn Umayyah, who was one of the three whose repentance Allah accepted. He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I found a man with my wife; I saw with my eyes and heard with my ears.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked what he had brought."

Hilal said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I see the aversion in your face at what I have informed you of, and Allah knows that I am truthful, and I said nothing but the truth." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Either the proof, or the legal punishment (hadd) upon you." The Ansar gathered and said: "We have been tested with what Sa'd said." While they were in that state, the revelation came down upon him, and when the revelation came down upon him his face would turn pale and redness would cover his body. When it had passed from him, he, peace be upon him, said: "Rejoice, O Hilal, for Allah has made a way out for you." He said: "I had been hoping for that from Allah, exalted is He." Then he recited these verses to them. He, peace be upon him, said: "Call her." She was called, and she denied what Hilal said. He, peace be upon him, said: "Allah knows that one of you two is a liar. Will any of you repent?" He commanded the mutual imprecation (mula'anah), and Hilal testified four testimonies: "By Allah, he is surely of the truthful." Then he, peace be upon him, said to him at the fifth: "Fear Allah, O Hilal, for the punishment of this world is easier than the punishment of the Hereafter." He said: "By Allah, Allah will not punish me for it, just as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not flog me," and he testified the fifth.

Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Will you testify?" She testified four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars. When she came to the fifth, he said to her: "Fear Allah, for the fifth is the one that makes it binding." She reflected for a moment and was inclined to confess, then she said: "By Allah, I will not disgrace my people," and she testified the fifth that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated the two of them, and said: "Watch her: if she brings forth a child who is ubayjij (having large eyes and a full face), asfar (of light reddish complexion), ahmash al-saqayn (thin-legged), then he belongs to Hilal; and if she brings forth one who is khadlaj al-saqayn (thick-calved), awral (of dark complexion), ja'd (curly-haired), then he belongs to her partner." She brought forth one who was awral and khadlaj al-saqayn. He, peace be upon him, said: "Had it not been for the oaths, there would have been a matter between me and her." 'Ikrimah said: "I saw him afterward as governor of one of the provinces, and he did not know who his father was!"

* * *

The Second Discussion: concerning the readings (qira'at). It was read as ﴿shahadah﴾ (witness) without the taa' (feminine), because the witnesses (shuhada') are a group, or because they are in the sense of the selves (anfusuhum). As for the one who reads arba' (four) in the accusative: it is in the position of an infinitive (masdar) and the governing element is the masdar which is "fa-shahadatu ahadihim," and it is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is omitted; so its estimate is "fa-wajibu shahadati ahadihim arba'a shahadat" (then obligatory is the testimony of one of them: four testimonies). It was also read as "anna la'nata Allah" and "anna ghadaba Allah" with the lightening of anna and the raising of what follows it. It was read as "an ghadiba Allahu," with the verb of anger (ghadiba). And it was read with the fifth in the accusative, in the sense of "wa-yashhadu al-khamisata" (and he testifies the fifth).

* * *

The Third Discussion: concerning the rulings, and the consideration of it relates to several parts.

The First Part: concerning what makes li'an binding, and it contains issues.

The first issue: Know that when a man accuses his wife of adultery, it is obligatory upon him the hadd if she is muhsanah (chaste/married), and the ta'zir (discretionary punishment) if she is not muhsanah, just as in accusing an unrelated woman, their consequence does not differ, except that they differ in the means of release. In slandering an unrelated person, the hadd does not fall from the slanderer except by the confession of the one slandered, or by evidence that establishes her adultery. In slandering a wife, the hadd falls from him by one of these two matters or by li'an. The Law only took li'an into account in this case and not with unrelated women for two reasons:

The first: there is no shame upon him in the adultery of an unrelated woman, and it is better for him to conceal it. But if he commits adultery with his wife, shame and a corrupt lineage fall upon him, so he cannot bear it, nor can he be held to the proof like one who apologizes. Therefore the Law specifically assigned this case to li'an.

The second: in the customary circumstances of a man with his wife, he generally does not intend to slander her except out of certainty; so when he accuses her, the accusation itself testifies to his truthfulness. However, the testimony of circumstance is not complete, so there is added to it what strengthens it of oaths, like the testimony of a woman: when it was weak, it was strengthened by increasing the number. A single witness is strengthened by an oath according to the opinion of many jurists.

The second issue: Abu Bakr al-Razi said: The hadd for slandering unrelated women and wives was flogging. The evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to Hilal ibn Umayyah when he slandered his wife with Sharik ibn Sahma': "Bring four who testify for you, or else a hadd upon your back." Thus it is established by this that the hadd for slandering wives was like the hadd for slandering unrelated women, except that flogging was abrogated (naskh) for spouses by li'an. A similar narration was related about the man who said: "What do you think, if a man found a man with his wife, if he speaks you flog him, if he kills you kill him, and if he remains silent he remains silent in rage." So these reports indicate that the hadd for slandering a wife was flogging, and that Allah abrogated it by li'an.

The third issue: al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: If a husband slanders his wife, then what is obligatory is the hadd, but the way of release from it is li'an, just as what is obligatory for slandering an unrelated woman is the hadd, and the way of release from it is witnesses. So if the husband refuses li'an, the hadd for slander binds him. If he performs li'an and the wife refuses li'an, the hadd for adultery binds her. Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: If the husband refuses li'an, he is imprisoned until he performs li'an; and likewise, if the wife refuses, she is imprisoned until she performs li'an. The proofs of al-Shafi'i are several:

The first: Allah, exalted is He, said at the beginning of the surah: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾ meaning other than wives, ﴿then do not produce four witnesses, flog them eighty lashes﴾. Then He joined to it the ruling on spouses, saying: ﴿And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves, then the testimony of one of them﴾ up to the verse. So just as the requirement for slandering unrelated women is to produce witnesses or be flogged, likewise the requirement for slandering wives is to produce li'an or the hadd.

The second: the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And it will avert the punishment from her﴾ "that she testify four testimonies by Allah." The alif and lam attached to "al-'adhab" (the punishment) do not indicate generality, because not all kinds of punishment became obligatory upon her, so they must be directed to the previously known referent (al-ma'hud al-sabiq). The previously known referent is the hadd, because He, exalted is He, mentioned at the beginning of the surah: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, and what is meant by it is the hadd. And when it is established that what is meant by "the punishment" in His saying ﴿it will avert the punishment from her﴾ is the hadd, it is established that if she does not perform li'an she would be flogged, and that by li'an she averts the hadd. If it is said: what is meant by the punishment is imprisonment. We say: We have already shown that the alif and lam are for the previously mentioned referent, and the nearest of what has been mentioned in this surah is "al-'adhab" in the sense of the hadd. Also, if we take it to mean the hadd, the verse does not become ambiguous; but if we take it to mean imprisonment, the verse becomes ambiguous, because the amount of imprisonment is not known.

The third: al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Among what indicates the invalidity of imprisonment with regard to the woman is that she says: "If the man is truthful, then flog me; and if he is a liar, then release me. What is my case with imprisonment? My imprisonment is not in the Book of Allah, nor in the Sunnah of His Messenger, nor in consensus (ijma'), nor in analogy (qiyas)."

The fourth: the husband slandered her, and did not bring a way out through the testimony of another or the testimony of himself; so the hadd became obligatory upon him, by His saying: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women, then do not produce four witnesses, flog them﴾. And if this is established regarding the man, it is established regarding the woman, because there is no one who makes a distinction.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 24, verses 6–10 (part 2 of 3)**

And the fifth: his saying, peace be upon him, to Khawla: "Then stoning is easier for you than the wrath of Allah." This is a text on the matter, and it is the proof of Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him. As for the woman's case, she did nothing except refrain from li'an (the mutual oath of cursing between spouses). This refraining is neither clear evidence of adultery nor an admission by her of it. Therefore it is not permissible to stone her, based on his saying, peace be upon him: "The blood of a man is not lawful…" the hadith. And if stoning is not required when she is muhsana (a married woman who is protected by a valid marriage), then flogging is not required for one who is not muhsana, because no one holds a distinction. Also, nukul (refusal to take the oath) is not explicit in admitting the charge, so the hadd (prescribed punishment) may not be established by it, like an ambiguous word that could mean adultery or something else.

**The fourth issue:** The majority said that if he says to her, "O adulteress," li'an becomes obligatory. Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said that he does not perform li'an unless he says, "I saw you committing adultery," or he denies a pregnancy she carries or a child from her. The majority's proof is that the generality of His saying, ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾, encompasses everyone. Also, there is no difference in accusing a non-related woman among all people, so likewise in the case of accusing a wife.

* * *

**The second part: the one who performs li'an.** Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Whoever's oath (yamin) is valid, his li'an is valid. Thus li'an takes place between two slaves, two dhimmis (non-Muslim subjects under Muslim protection), and two people who have been subjected to hadd. Likewise if one of them is a slave, or if the husband is Muslim and the wife is a dhimmi. Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said that it is not valid in two cases. The first: that the wife is one for whom the hadd is not required upon her accuser if he were a stranger, such as when the wife is a slave or a dhimmi.

The second: that one of them is not among the people of testimony (shahada), such as one who has been subjected to hadd for qadhf (false accusation of unchastity), or a slave, or a disbeliever. Then he claimed that a fasiq (one who is openly sinful) and a blind man, even though neither of them is among the people of testimony, may perform li'an validly. The basis of al-Shafi'i's view, may Allah have mercy on him, is that the apparent meaning of His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ encompasses all, and there is no meaning to restricting it. Analogy (qiyas) is also apparent in two respects:

The first: the purpose is to ward off shame from oneself, and to ward off the child of adultery from oneself. Just as a non-hadd person needs this, so too a hadd person needs it.

The second: we are agreed that li'an is valid for a fasiq and a blind man, even though neither of them is among the people of testimony. Likewise the matter is for others. The common element (jami') is the need to ward off the shame of adultery.

The view of Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, rests on text and meaning. As for the text, what 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As related: that he, peace be upon him, said: "Four kinds of women have no li'an between them and their husbands: a Jewish woman and a Christian woman under a Muslim, a free woman under a slave, and a slave woman under a free man."

As for the meaning, we say: in the first case, the obligation upon one who accuses a wife or a stranger was the hadd, by His saying: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾. Then this was abrogated (naskh) for husbands, and li'an was put in its place. So when li'an with husbands stands in place of the hadd for strangers' accusations, li'an is not obligatory upon one on whom the hadd would not be obligatory if a stranger accused her. As for the second case, the view is that li'an is a testimony (shahada), so it must not be valid except from people of testimony. We said that li'an is a testimony for two reasons:

The first: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And they have no witnesses except themselves, so the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah﴾. So Allah named their li'an a testimony, as He said: ﴿And call upon two witnesses from your men﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282], and He said: ﴿Call upon four witnesses from among you against them﴾ [al-Nisa': 15].

The second: when he, peace be upon him, performed li'an between the spouses, he commanded them to perform it with the wording of testimony (shahada), and did not restrict it to the wording of oath (yamin). If it is established that li'an is a testimony, then it must be that the testimony of one subjected to hadd for qadhf is not accepted, based on His saying: ﴿And do not accept their testimony ever﴾ [al-Nur: 4]. And if this is established for one subjected to hadd, it is established for a slave and a disbeliever too, either by consensus that they are not among the people of testimony, or because no one holds a distinction.

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, replied that li'an is not testimony in reality; rather it is an oath, because a person may not testify for himself. Also, if it were testimony, the woman would have to bring eight testimonies, because she is half of a man in this regard. Also, it is valid from a blind man and a fasiq, yet their testimony is not accepted. If it is said that a fasiq and a fasiqa may repent, we say: likewise a slave may be freed, and then his testimony is accepted. Then al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, emphasized: when a slave is freed, his testimony is accepted immediately, whereas when a fasiq repents, his testimony is not accepted immediately. Then he held Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, to the argument that the testimony of dhimmis is accepted against one another, so li'an between a dhimmi man and a dhimmi woman should be valid. This is all the words of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him.

He then said after that: hudud (prescribed punishments) differ according to the person to whom they apply. The meaning is that if the husband does not perform li'an, the hadd for qadhf is halved for him because of his slavery. If he performs li'an and she does not perform li'an, her hadd differs according to her ihsan (chastity/protected status), her lack of ihsan, her freedom, and her slavery.

* * *

**The third part: the rulings that follow from li'an.** Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: five rulings are connected to li'an: the averting of the hadd, the negation of the child's paternity, separation (furqa), permanent prohibition (tahrim mu'abbad), and the obligation of the hadd upon her. All of these are established by his li'an alone, and it does not depend on her li'an or on a ruling of a judge (hakim). For the ruling of the judge concerning it is an execution (tanfidh) from him, not the initiation of separation. So let us discuss these issues:

**The first issue:** The mujtahids (qualified jurists) differed on whether separation occurs through li'an, in four views:

First: 'Uthman al-Batti said: I do not see that the husband's li'an with his wife requires anything that would obligate him to divorce her.

Second: Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said: separation does not occur upon their finishing li'an until the judge separates them.

Third: Malik, al-Layth and Zufar, may Allah have mercy on them, said: when they finish li'an, separation occurs even if the judge does not separate them.

Fourth: al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: when the husband completes the testimony and the li'an, his wife's bed (firash) is removed, and she is never lawful to him again, whether she performs li'an or not.

The proofs of 'Uthman al-Batti are several:

The first: li'an is neither explicit nor allusive (kinaya) regarding separation. Therefore it must not produce separation, like the other statements that have no indication of separation. For at most, it means that the husband is truthful in his statement, and that does not require prohibition. Do you not see that if evidence were established against her, that would not require prohibition? So if he is lying and she is truthful, it is established that there is no indication in it of prohibition.

The second: if they performed li'an between themselves, it would not require separation; likewise if they performed li'an before the judge.

The third: li'an stands in place of witnesses in the accusation of strangers. Just as there is no benefit in bringing witnesses there except to drop the hadd, likewise li'an has no effect except to drop the hadd.

The fourth: if the husband retracts his accusation of her and is then subjected to hadd, that does not require separation. Likewise if he performs li'an, because li'an stands in place of averting the hadd.

He said: As for the Prophet's ﷺ separation between the two who performed li'an, that was in the case of al-'Ajlani, and he had divorced her three times after the li'an, so for that reason he separated them. As for the view of Abu Hanifa, which is that the judge separates them, two matters must be explained:

One: it is obligatory upon the judge to separate them. Its proof is what Sahl ibn Sa'd related in the case of al-'Ajlani: "The sunnah has passed concerning the two who performed li'an, that they be separated and never come together again."

The second: separation does not occur except by the judgment of the judge. They argued for this with several points:

The first: it was narrated in the case of 'Uwaymir that when they finished, "'Uwaymir said: 'I have lied against her, O Messenger of Allah, if I keep her; she is divorced three times,' and he divorced her three times before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him." The argument from this report is in several respects:

The first: if separation had occurred through li'an, his saying "I have lied against her if I keep her" would be void, because keeping her would be impossible.

The second: what is narrated in this report, that he divorced her three divorces, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ executed it. The execution of divorce is only possible if separation had not occurred by the li'an itself.

The third: what Sahl ibn Sa'd said in this report: "The sunnah has passed concerning the two who performed li'an, that they be separated and never come together again." If separation had occurred by li'an, separating them afterward would be impossible.

The second: Abu Bakr al-Razi said: al-Shafi'i's view opposes the verse, because if separation occurred by the husband's li'an, the woman would perform li'an even though she is a stranger, and that opposes the verse, because Allah only obligated li'an between spouses.

The third: li'an is a testimony, whose ruling is not established except before a judge. Therefore it must not produce separation except by the judgment of a judge, just as what is testified to is not established except by the judgment of a judge.

The fourth: through li'an the woman acquires her own right, just as the claimant acquires his claim by evidence. Since the claimant may not acquire his claim except by the judgment of a judge, the same must apply to the woman acquiring her right.

The fifth: li'an has no indication of prohibition, because at most it states that she committed adultery. If evidence were established of her adultery, or she confessed to it, that would not require prohibition. Likewise li'an. When there is no indication in it of prohibition, separation must not occur by it. So separation must be brought about, either by the husband or by the judge.

As for the view of Malik and Zufar, their proof is that if the two agreed to remain married, they would not be left together but would be separated. This shows that li'an has obligated separation.

As for al-Shafi'i's view, may Allah have mercy on him, he has two proofs:

The first: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And she averts the punishment from herself by testifying﴾ and so on. This shows that the wife's li'an has no effect except in averting punishment from herself, and that all rulings obligated by li'an have occurred by the husband's li'an.

The second: the husband's li'an alone is independently sufficient to negate the child's paternity. Therefore the consideration must be his statement regarding attributing the child, not her statement. Do you not see that in her li'an she attributes the child to him, while we negate it from him? So the husband's negation is considered, not the wife's attribution. This is why, if the husband retracts his accusation, the child is attributed to him; and as long as he persists in li'an, the child is negated from him. Since it is established that his li'an is independently sufficient to negate the child, it must be independently sufficient for the occurrence of separation. For if separation did not occur, the child would not be negated, given His saying, peace be upon him: "The child belongs to the bed (firash)." As long as the bed remains, the child is attributed to it. So when the child is negated from him by his li'an alone, it must be that the bed is removed from him by his li'an alone.

As for the reports which Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, used as evidence, they mean that the Prophet, peace be upon him, informed of the occurrence of separation and ruled by it, and that does not preclude that the cause of separation was something else.

As for the analogies he mentioned, they rest on the premise that li'an is testimony, and the matter is not so; rather it is an oath, as we have explained. As for his statement that li'an has no indication of the occurrence of prohibition, we say: its evidence is in negating the child, which is accepted, and negating the child implies negating the lawfulness of marriage. And Allah knows best.

**The second issue:** Malik, al-Shafi'i, Abu Yusuf, al-Thawri, Ishaq and al-Hasan said: the two who performed li'an may never come together again. This is also the view of 'Ali, 'Umar and Ibn Mas'ud. Abu Hanifa and Muhammad said: if he retracts his accusation and is subjected to the hadd, the prohibition of the contract ceases, and she becomes lawful to him through a new marriage. The proofs of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, are several matters:

[p. 149]

First: the Prophet's ﷺ saying to the one who performed li'an (mutual oaths of condemnation), after the li'an was completed, "You have no claim over her" (ﷺ), without adding "until you retract your accusation." Had retraction been the condition for ending this prohibition, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have restricted it to that condition, just as he said regarding the woman divorced three times: ﴿So if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾ [al-Baqarah: 230].

Second: what is narrated from 'Ali, 'Umar and Ibn Mas'ud, that they said, "The two who have performed li'an never reunite, ever." This has also been narrated as a marfu' report traced to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Third: what al-Zuhri narrated from Sahl ibn Sa'd concerning the story of al-'Ajlani: "The sunnah has passed that when the two perform li'an, they are separated, and then they never reunite, ever." This is the proof of Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him), along with the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And lawful to you is what is beyond that﴾ and His words: ﴿So marry what is good for you﴾.

Third issue: The scholars agree that a child may be disowned from the husband through li'an. It is reported from some deviant individuals that the child belongs to the husband and that his lineage is not severed by li'an, and they cited the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "The child belongs to the bed." This view is weak, because the reports indicating that lineage is severed by li'an are like the mutawatir (widely transmitted) reports, so this single report cannot oppose them.

Fourth issue: al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: if one of the two spouses utters only some of the words of li'an, the ruling does not apply to them. Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him) said: most of the words of li'an act as the whole when the judge rules by it. The stronger view is that of al-Shafi'i, because it indicates that the woman cannot avert the punishment from herself except by completing what Allah the Exalted mentioned. Whoever holds otherwise does so on the basis of a separate proof.

* * *

Fifth section: On the manner of li'an. The verse explicitly indicates it. The man testifies four times by Allah, saying: "I testify by Allah that I am truthful regarding what I have accused her of, namely adultery." Then he says: "And the curse of Allah be upon me if I am among the liars." According to al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him), five rulings are connected to the husband's li'an. If the woman wishes to avert the punishment for adultery from herself, she must perform li'an, and only this one ruling is connected to her li'an. Here are some branches:

First branch: They agree that li'an is like testimony, so it is not established except before a judge.

Second branch: al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: the man is made to stand while he testifies, and the woman remains seated; the woman is made to stand while she testifies, and the man remains seated. The imam orders someone to place his hand over the man's mouth when he reaches the words about the curse and wrath, and says to him: "I fear that if you are not truthful, you will incur the curse of Allah."

Third branch: li'an may be performed in Mecca between al-Maqam and al-Rukn; in Medina, at the minbar; in Jerusalem, in its mosque; and elsewhere in the honored places. The li'an of a polytheist is the same as that of others in its manner. As for the time, it is Friday after the 'asr prayer. A group of notable persons must be present, the least of whom are four.

* * *

Sixth section: On the remaining benefits, and it contains issues.

First issue: Our companions (the Shafi'is/Ash'aris) used this verse to refute the view of the Khawarij (the Kharijites), that adultery and false accusation of adultery are kufr (disbelief), on two grounds:

First: If the accuser is truthful, she is an adulteress; if he is lying, he is a slanderer. So according to their view, disbelief must occur from one of the two. That would be apostasy, and it would follow that separation occurs and there is no li'an at all, and that it would be a separation by apostasy, so that no inheritance could ever be connected to it.

Second: If disbelief were established against her through his li'an, then she would have to be killed, not flogged or stoned, because the punishment of an apostate is distinct from the hadd (prescribed punishment) for adultery.

Second issue: The verse indicates the falsity of the view of one who says that the occurrence of adultery invalidates the marriage. This is because, if he accuses her of adultery, his statement must be as if he acknowledges the invalidity of the marriage, so that his position would be like that of one who acknowledges that she is his foster sister or that she is a disbeliever. If it were so, separation would have to occur by the mere accusation before li'an, and the invalidity of that has been established by consensus.

[p. 150]

Third issue: The Mu'tazila said: the verse indicates that the slanderer deserves the curse of Allah the Exalted if he is lying, and that he has committed fisq (grave sin). Likewise, the adulterer and the adulteress deserve the wrath and punishment of Allah the Exalted; otherwise it would not be proper for them to curse themselves, just as it is not permissible for anyone to ask his Lord to curse children and the insane. If that is valid, then he has deserved punishment, and punishment is permanent like reward, and they cannot coexist, so their reward is also nullified. Therefore, if they do not repent, it is not permissible for them to enter Paradise, because the community agrees that whoever among the obligated enters Paradise is rewarded for his acts of obedience, and that indicates the eternal abiding of the sinners in the Fire. Our companions said: we do not concede that being under wrath because of his sin contradicts being pleased with him for the sake of his faith. Even if we concede that, we do not concede that only one who deserves reward enters Paradise. And the consensus is disputed.

Fourth issue: The woman performing li'an was singled out to be subjected to five oaths with the wrath of Allah, as a heightening of severity upon her, because she is the root of immorality and its source, through her vanity and her desires. For this reason she is mentioned first in the verse about flogging.

Know that when He, glorified is He, explained the ruling for one who accuses chaste women and married women as we have mentioned, and there was in that a mercy and a blessing that is not hidden, because He, the Exalted, made through li'an a way for the man to reach his aim, and a way for her to avert the punishment from herself, and for both of them a way to repentance and turning back, then for this reason He, the Exalted, explained by His words: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾ [al-Nur: 14] the magnitude of His blessings in what He explained of these rulings, and in what He granted respite and preserved, and enabled for repentance. There is no doubt that there is an ellipsis in the speech, since an answer must exist; however, omitting it indicates that it is a great matter that cannot be fathomed, and many an unspoken matter is more eloquent than a spoken one.

The Fifth Ruling: The Story of the Slander (al-Ifk)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you. Do not consider it bad for you; rather, it is good for you. For every person among them is what he earned of the sin, and he who undertook most of it among them will have a great punishment.﴾

The discussion of this verse concerns two aspects:

The first: its interpretation (tafsir).

The second: the occasion of its revelation (sabab al-nuzul).

As for the interpretation, know that Allah, exalted is He, mentions three things in this verse. The first: He relates the event, which is His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you.﴾ *Al-ifk* is the most intense form of lying and fabrication. It has been said that it is *al-buhtan* (fabricated slander), which is a matter that you are not aware of until it surprises you. Its root is *al-ifk*, meaning turning, because it is a statement turned away from its true face. The Muslims agreed that what is meant by what was fabricated is the accusation against ʿĀʾisha. Allah described that lie as *ifk* because what was known of ʿĀʾisha's condition was contrary to it, for several reasons:

The first: that her being the wife of the Messenger (ﷺ), who is protected from sin, prevents this. The prophets are sent to the disbelievers to call them and to win their hearts, so it is necessary that nothing be with them that would repel them. And a man's wife being openly unchaste is among the greatest repellents. If it is said: how could the wife of a Prophet be a disbeliever, like the wife of Noah and Lot, but it was not permitted for her to be unchaste? And also, if that were not permitted, the Messenger would have been the one most aware of her abstention, and if he knew that, his heart would not have been distressed, nor would he have asked ʿĀʾisha about the details of the event. We say: the answer to the first is that disbelief is not among the repellents, whereas her being unchaste is among the repellents. The answer to the second is that he (peace be upon him) often felt distress in his heart because of the statements of the disbelievers, while knowing the corruption of those statements. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We know that your breast is constricted by what they say﴾ [al-Hijr: 97], so this was of this kind.

The second: that what was known of ʿĀʾisha's condition before that event was only chastity and distance from the causes of immorality, and whoever is like that, the fitting thing is to think well of her.

The third: that the slanderers were from among the hypocrites and their followers, and it is known that the speech of a hostile fabricator is a kind of delirium. So, by the combination of these indications, that statement was known to be false before the revelation descended.

As for *al-ʿusba*, it has been said that it is a group from ten to forty, and likewise *al-ʿişaba*; *iʿṣawṣabū* means they gathered. They were ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the head of hypocrisy; Zayd ibn Rifaʿa; Hassan ibn Thabit; Mistah ibn Uthatha; Hamna bint Jahsh; and those who assisted them.

As for His saying ﴿among you﴾, the meaning is that those who brought the lie concerning the matter of ʿĀʾisha were a group from among you, O believers, because ʿAbd Allah was among those who were judged to be believers outwardly.

The fourth: that He, glorified is He, explained the condition of the one who was slandered and those connected to her with His saying: ﴿Do not consider it bad for you; rather, it is good for you.﴾ The correct view is that this address is not to the slanderers, but to those whom they slandered and harmed. If it is said that this is problematic for two reasons:

One: that they had not been previously mentioned.

Two: that the two who were slandered are ʿĀʾisha and Ṣafwan, so how can the plural form in His saying ﴿Do not consider it bad for you﴾ be applied to them?

The answer to the first: they were mentioned earlier in His saying ﴿among you﴾. The answer to the second: what is meant by the plural term is everyone who was harmed by that lie and grieved over it. It is known that he (ﷺ) was harmed by it, and likewise Abu Bakr and those connected to him. If it is said: in what respect does it become good for them, when it is a harm in the immediate term? We say, for several reasons:

The first: they endured that grief seeking the pleasure of Allah, exalted is He, and so they earned reward by it, and this is the way of the believers when injustice befalls them.

The second: had they not made the slander public, the accusation could have remained hidden in the hearts of some, but at the time of its publication the falsehood of the people was exposed over the course of time.

The third: it became good for them because of the honor and demonstration of their merit it contains, in that eighteen verses were revealed, each one of which independently established the innocence of ʿĀʾisha. Allah, exalted is He, bore witness to the falsehood of the slanderers, attributed them to the fabrication, and made it obligatory to curse and blame them. This is the utmost honor and virtue.

The fourth: her situation became one in which disbelief and faith were tied to her condemnation and praise. When Allah, exalted is He, explicitly stated that that event was a fabrication and elaborated on it, then everyone who doubted it was definitely a disbeliever. This is a lofty rank. Among the people there are those who said that His saying ﴿Do not consider it bad for you﴾ is an address to the slanderers, and Allah, exalted is He, made it good for them for several reasons:

The first: the Qur'an that was revealed became a barrier preventing them from persisting in it, so it became a cutting off for them from continuing this fabrication.

The second: it became good for them in that this mention was a hastened punishment, like an expiation (kaffara).

The third: it became good for them in that some of them repented before Him. Know that this view is weak, because He addressed them with the second person pronoun (kāf), and when He described the people of the slander, He made the address in the third person (hāʾ) with His saying, exalted is He:

[Page 152]

﴿For every person among them is what he earned of the sin.﴾ It is known that what they earned itself is not a punishment. So what is meant is the requital of what they earned of punishment in the Hereafter and blame in this world. The meaning is that the measure of punishment is like the measure of their plunging into it.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿and he who undertook most of it among them will have a great punishment,﴾ there are several issues:

The first issue: *kibrahu* has been read with a *ḍamma* and with a *kasra*, and it means its greatness (ʿiẓamuhu).

The second issue: al-Ḍaḥḥak said: the one who undertook most of it was Hassan and Mistah, and the Messenger (ﷺ) flogged both of them when Allah revealed her innocence. He also flogged with them a woman from Quraysh. It is narrated that ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her) mentioned Hassan and said: "I hope for Paradise for him." It was said to her: "Is he not the one who undertook most of it?" She said: "When I hear his poetry in praise of the Messenger, I hope Paradise for him." And the Messenger (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed Allah supports Hassan with the Holy Spirit in his poetry." In another narration: "And what punishment is more severe than blindness?" Perhaps Allah made that great punishment the loss of his sight. The more likely reading is that what is meant by it is ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, for he was a hypocrite who sought what would be a disparagement of the Messenger (peace be upon him), and the others were followers of him in what he did. Among them were also those who were not accused of hypocrisy.

The third issue: attributing the greatness to him means that he was the initiator of that statement, so he necessarily received the same punishment as everyone who said that, in accordance with his (peace be upon him) saying: "Whoever establishes an evil practice, upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it until the Day of Resurrection." It has also been said that the reason for that attribution is his intense eagerness to spread that immorality, and this is the view of Abu Muslim.

The fourth issue: al-Jubba'i said: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿For every person among them is what he earned of the sin﴾ means the punishment for what he earned. If they did not deserve punishment for that, it would not be permissible for Allah, exalted is He, to say that. And in it is an indication that whoever among them does not repent will go to the everlasting punishment in the Hereafter, because with the deserving of punishment, deserving of reward is not permissible. The answer: the discussion of nullification (*muhabata*) has passed more than once, so there is no point in repeating it, and Allah knows best.

As for the occasion of revelation: al-Zuhri narrated from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, ʿAlqama ibn Abi Waqqas, and ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUtba ibn Masʿud, all of whom narrated from ʿĀʾisha, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended a journey, he drew lots among his wives, and whichever one's name came out, he took her with him. She said: He drew lots among us in a campaign he undertook before the campaign of Banu al-Mustaliq, and my name came out, so I went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). That was after the revelation of the verse of the hijab, so I was carried in a howdah. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned and drew near to Medina, he stopped at a place, then announced the departure. I stood up when they announced the departure and walked until I passed the army. When I finished my need and returned to my mount, I touched my chest and found that my necklace of Zafar stones had broken. So I went back and searched for my necklace, and its search detained me.

The men who used to load me came and lifted my howdah, thinking that I was inside it, because of my lightness, for I was a young girl of tender age. So they thought I was in the howdah and departed with the camel. When I returned I did not find anyone at the place, so I sat down and said: perhaps they will return looking for me. Then I slept. Safwan ibn al-Muʿattal used to remain in the army, following up on people's belongings and carrying them to the next stopping place, so that nothing would be lost from them. When he saw me he recognized me, and said: 'What has kept you from the people?' So I told him the story. He dismounted and withdrew until I mounted, then he led the camel. The people, when they stopped, missed me, and there was commotion about my matter. While the people were in that state, I came upon them, and the people spoke and gossiped about my story. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Medina, and I was afflicted with an illness, and I did not notice from him (peace be upon him) the gentleness I used to know from him when I was ill. He would only enter, then say: 'How are you?' That is what troubled me, and I did not yet perceive what had happened until I recovered. I went out one night with Umm Mistah for a matter of ours. Then Umm Mistah and I came back toward my house when we had finished our business. Umm Mistah stumbled over her cloak and said: 'Mistah has perished!' I denied that and said: 'Do you curse a man who witnessed Badr?' She said: 'Have you not heard the news?' I said: 'And what is it?' She said: 'I testify that you are one of the believing women who are heedless.' Then she told me of the words of the people of the slander, and my illness increased upon my illness. I returned weeping. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon me and said: 'How are you?' I said: 'Permit me to go to my parents.' He permitted me, and I came to my parents and said to my mother: 'O mother, what are the people talking about?' She said: 'O daughter, ease your mind, for by Allah, rarely is a beautiful woman with a husband who loves her and who has co-wives, without the co-wives making much of it against her.' Then she said: 'Did you not know what was said until now?' So I began to weep, and I wept that night, then I woke up weeping. My father entered upon me while I was weeping, and he said to my mother: 'What is making her weep?' She said: 'She did not know what was said about her until now.' He began to weep and said: 'Be quiet, daughter.'

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned ʿAlī ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and Usama ibn Zayd and consulted them about separating from his family. Usama said: 'O Messenger of Allah, they are your family, and we know nothing but good.' As for ʿAlī, he said: 'Allah has not constricted things for you, and there are many women other than her. But if you ask the slave girl, she will tell you the truth.' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called Barira and asked her about my matter. Barira said: 'O Messenger of Allah, by the One who sent you with the truth, I have never seen anything in her more than that she is a young girl of tender age who sleeps over her family's dough until the domestic animal comes and eats it.' She said: Then the Prophet (ﷺ) stood up on the pulpit and said: 'O assembly of Muslims, who will excuse me regarding a man whose harm has reached me concerning my family?' meaning ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy. 'By Allah, I know nothing about my family but good.'"

And indeed they mentioned a man, and I knew of him nothing but good, and he never entered upon my household except with me. Then Sa'd ibn Mu'adh stood up and said: "I will excuse you, O Messenger of Allah, from him. If he is from the Aws, I will strike off his neck; and if he is from our brothers of the Khazraj, then you need only command us, and we will do it." Then Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah stood up, and he was the chief of the Khazraj, and he was a righteous man, but zealous partisanship (al-hamiyyah) seized him, and he said to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh: "You have lied; by Allah, you will not be able to kill him." Then Usayd ibn Hudayr stood up, and he was the cousin of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and he said: "You have lied; by the life of Allah, we will certainly kill him, and you are indeed a hypocrite who argues on behalf of the hypocrites." Then the two tribes, the Aws and the Khazraj, were stirred up, until they were about to fight one another, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was on the pulpit, and he did not cease calming them until they fell silent.
