She said: "I remained that day weeping, my tears not ceasing for me, and my parents thought that weeping would split my liver. Then, while they were sitting with me and I was weeping, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon us, greeted us with peace, and sat down." She said: "He had not sat with me since what was said about me was said, and he had remained a month without Allah revealing anything to him concerning my affair."

Then he said: "As to what follows, O 'A'ishah, it has reached me that such-and-such was said about you. If you are innocent, Allah the Exalted will clear you; and if you have committed a sin, then seek forgiveness of Allah and repent to Him, for when the servant repents, Allah turns to him in forgiveness."

She said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished his speech, my tears ceased flowing. Then I said to my father: 'Answer the Messenger of Allah on my behalf.' He said: 'By Allah, I do not know what to say.' So I said to my mother: 'Answer the Messenger of Allah on my behalf.' She said: 'By Allah, I do not know what to say.' So I said, while I was a young girl of tender age who did not recite much of the Qur'an: 'Indeed, by Allah, I know that you have heard this until it has settled in your souls and you have believed it. So if I tell you that I am innocent, you will not believe me; and if I confess to you a matter while Allah knows that I am innocent, you will believe me. By Allah, I find for myself and for you no example except that of the righteous servant, Abu Yusuf'—and I did not mention his name—'﴿So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the one sought for help against what you describe﴾.'"

She said: "Then I turned over and lay down on my bed, and I, by Allah, knew that Allah the Exalted would clear me. But by Allah, I did not think that a revelation would be sent down concerning my affair that would be recited, for my affair was too insignificant in my own estimation for Allah to speak about me in a matter that would be recited. Rather, I hoped that the Messenger of Allah would see in a dream a vision by which Allah would clear me."

She said: "By Allah, the Messenger of Allah did not rise from his place, and no one left the household, until Allah sent down the revelation upon His Prophet. He was seized by what used to seize him when revelation descended, so that drops like pearls of sweat would roll from him even on a cold day, from the weight of the revelation. He was covered with a garment, and a cushion was placed under his head. By Allah, I was not frightened, nor did I care, for I knew of my innocence. As for my parents, by Allah, they were nearly beside themselves, thinking that their souls would leave their bodies out of fear that Allah would bring about the confirmation of what the people had said. Then, when the Messenger of Allah was relieved of it, he was smiling, and the first word he spoke was: 'Rejoice, O 'A'ishah, for by Allah, Allah has indeed cleared you.'" I said: "Praise be to Allah, not to you, nor to your companions." My mother said: "Stand up and go to him." I said: "By Allah, I will not stand up to him, nor will I praise anyone except Allah, who sent down my innocence."

So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a faction among you﴾, the ten verses. Then Abu Bakr said: "By Allah, I will no longer spend on Mistah after this," though he had been spending on him because of his kinship to him and his poverty. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the near of kin﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Would you not like Allah to forgive you?﴾. Abu Bakr said: "Yes, by Allah, I would like Allah to forgive me," and so he resumed the spending on Mistah. She said: "When my innocence was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood on the pulpit, mentioned that, and recited the Qur'an. When he came down, he had 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, Mistah, Hamnah, and Hassan given the prescribed punishment (hadd)."

Know that when the Exalted, glorified is He, mentioned the story, and mentioned the condition of the slandered and the slanderers, He followed it with what is fitting for it of etiquettes and deterrents, and these are of several kinds:

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 24, verses 12–14:

[Page 155]

The first type: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and the believing women not think well of one another and say, "This is a clear lie"?﴾

This is one of the courtesies (adab) that they were obliged to observe. "Lawla" (لَوْلا) means "halla" (why not / would that), and this is common in the language when a verb follows it, as in His saying: ﴿Why did You not delay me...﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 10] and His saying: ﴿Why was there not a town that believed...﴾ [Yunus: 98]. When a noun follows it, the usage is different, as in His saying: ﴿Had it not been for you, we would have been believers﴾ [Saba: 31] and His saying: ﴿Had it not been for Allah's favour upon you and His mercy...﴾ [al-Nur: 10]. The meaning is: it was obligatory upon the believers, when they heard the words of the slanderer, to deny them, to occupy themselves with thinking well (of the accused), and not to rush to accusation regarding one whom they knew to be pure. Here there are questions:

The first question: Why was it not said, "Why, when you heard it, did you not think well of yourselves and say...?" Why did He shift from direct address to the third person, and from the pronoun to the noun?

The answer: It is to intensify the rebuke through the device of iltifat (shift of grammatical person, i.e., from address to third-person reference). The explicit mention of the word "believers" indicates that sharing in faith requires that nothing but good be thought of Muslims, because his religion decrees that sin is a source of harm, and his reason guides him to the obligation of avoiding harm. This necessitates a strong presumption that he avoids sin. When this presumption favouring avoidance exists, and no opposing indicator of equal strength is present, it is obligatory to think well (of him), and it is forbidden to proceed to disparagement.

The second question: What is meant by His saying "bi-anfusihim" (with/about themselves)? The answer has two aspects:

The first: What is meant is that some of them should think well of others. A parallel is His saying: ﴿do not defame one another﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11], and His saying: ﴿kill yourselves﴾ [al-Baqara: 54], and His saying: ﴿when you enter houses, greet one another﴾ [al-Nur: 61]. The meaning is: with those like yourselves among the believers, who are as your own selves.

It has been related that Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (may Allah be pleased with him) said to his wife Umm Ayyub: "Do you not see what is being said?" She replied: "If you were in place of Safwan, would you have thought ill of the sanctuary of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "No." She said: "And if I were in place of Aisha, I would not have betrayed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Aisha is better than me, and Safwan is better than you."

Ibn Zayd said that this is a reproach to the believers, since a believer does not commit fornication with his mother, nor does a mother with her son, and Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) is the Mother of the Believers.

The second: He made the believers like a single soul regarding what befalls it. So when something disagreeable befalls one of them, it is as if it befalls all of them. From al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said, (peace be upon him): "The likeness of the Muslims in their mutual kindness, compassion and sympathy is like that of a body: when one part of it suffers with sleeplessness and fever, the whole body suffers." And from Abu Burda, who said, (peace be upon him): "The believers to one another are like a building, one part of which strengthens another."

The third question: What is the meaning of His saying "This is a clear lie," and is it permissible for one who hears what he does not know to say that? The answer is in two respects.

The first: Yes, one must say that, but he reports it as the statement of the slanderer, which is not supported by any indication, and not as the reality of a matter he does not know.

The second: That is obligatory in the matter of Aisha, because her being the wife of the Messenger (ﷺ), who is protected from all repellent things, serves as a conclusive proof that this is a lie. Abu Bakr al-Razi said: This indicates that it is obligatory, regarding one whose apparent state is uprightness, to think well of him, and it necessitates that the contracts and dealings of Muslims be understood as valid and permissible. For this reason our companions (the Hanafi scholars) said about one who finds a man with a foreign woman and both confess to being married: it is not permissible to disbelieve the two of them, rather it is obligatory to believe them. Malik held that he should inflict the hadd punishment on both if they do not produce evidence of the marriage contract. Likewise, our companions (may Allah be pleased with them) said regarding one who sells a dirham and a dinar for two dirhams and two dinars, that the two exchanges are to be differentiated, because we have been commanded to think well of believers, so it is necessary to interpret it as what is permissible, which is the differentiation between them. Similarly, if he sells a decorated sword containing one hundred dirhams for two hundred dirhams, we treat the hundred as matched with the hundred and the excess as being for the sword. This also indicates the view of Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him) that Muslims are upright (adl) so long as no doubt appears about them, because we are commanded to think well, and this necessitates accepting testimony so long as no doubt appears about him that would require suspending or rejecting it. He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Surely conjecture avails nothing against the truth﴾ [Yunus: 36].

* * *

(﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it? Since they did not bring the witnesses, then they, in the sight of Allah, are the liars.﴾ ﴿Had it not been for Allah's bounty upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into.﴾)

The second type: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it? Since they did not bring the witnesses, then they, in the sight of Allah, are the liars.﴾

This is of the category of zawajir (admonitions). The meaning is: why did they not bring, for what they mentioned, four witnesses who testify to having witnessed what they accused her of? ﴿Since they did not bring the witnesses﴾ means: since they did not establish evidence for what they said. ﴿Then they, in the sight of Allah﴾ means: in His judgment, ﴿they are the liars.﴾ If it is asked: Is it not the case that, when they do not bring witnesses, it is possible that they are truthful just as it is possible that they are liars, so why did He definitively judge them to be liars? The answer has two aspects:

The first: What is meant by this are those who accused Aisha specifically, and they were, in the sight of Allah, liars.

The second: What is meant is that "those, in the sight of Allah," are in the position of liars, because a liar must be restrained from lying, and the slanderer, if he does not bring witnesses, must be restrained. Since his situation is like that of a liar in needing restraint, the term "liar" is applied to him figuratively (majaz).

[Page 156]

The third type: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Had it not been for Allah's bounty upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into.﴾

This is also of the category of admonitions. Here "lawla" (لَوْلا) indicates the prevention of one thing due to the existence of another. It is said: he "afada fi al-hadith" (plunged into speech), "indafa'a" (rushed on), and "khada" (waded into). There are two aspects to the meaning:

The first: Had it not been that I decreed to bestow upon you favours in this world of various kinds, among which is granting you respite for repentance, and to show mercy to you in the Hereafter by pardon and forgiveness, I would have hastened to punish you for what you waded into of the story of the slander.

The second: Had it not been for Allah's bounty upon you and His mercy, a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into, both in this world and in the Hereafter together. In this case there is inversion (taqdim and ta'khir) in the verse. The address is to the slanderers, and this is the view of Muqatil. This bounty is the judgment of Allah, Exalted is He, in delaying the punishment and in deciding to accept repentance from whoever repents.

The meaning of "talaqqawnahu" (you received it) is that some of you take it from others. It is said: talaqqa al-qawl, talaqqanahu, and talaqqafahu (he received the saying). From this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words﴾ [al-Baqarah: 37]. It has been read according to the original form as "tatalaqqawnahu" and "italaqqawnahu" with the dhal assimilated into the ta' (idgham). "Talaqqawnahu" may also come from laqiyahu, meaning lafiqahu (to take up, to pick up). "Tulqunahu" comes from iilqa' (casting), i.e., some of them casting it upon others. "Tilqunahu" and "ta'liqunahu" come from al-walq and al-alq, which mean lying. "Tilqunahu" is reported from Aisha. And from Sufyan: "I heard my mother reading idh tathaqqafunahu," and her father used to recite according to the reading of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.

Know that Allah, exalted is He, described them as committing three sins, and attached to them the touch of a tremendous punishment. The first: receiving the slander with their tongues. This is because a man would meet another man and say to him, "What is behind you?" and he would relate to him the story of the slander, until it spread and became well known, so that no house and no gathering remained without it flying into it. It is as if they strove to spread the foul deed, and that is among the grave matters.

The second: they were speaking about what they had no knowledge of. This indicates that it is not permissible to report anything except with knowledge. As for what the truth of which is not known, reporting it is like reporting what is known to be false, in terms of prohibition. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge﴾ [al-Isra': 36]. If it is asked: what is the meaning of His saying "with your mouths," since speech only occurs with the mouth? We say: its meaning is that a known matter has its knowledge in the heart, and then it is expressed by the tongue. This slander is nothing but a saying that runs on your tongues without knowledge of it arising in the heart, like His saying: ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾ [Al 'Imran: 167].

The third: they considered it a small matter, while it is one of the great grave matters. It indicates three things:

The first: it indicates that slander is among the major sins, by His saying: ﴿while it is, in the sight of Allah, tremendous.﴾

The second: by His saying: ﴿and you thought it a trivial matter﴾ he alerted that the magnitude of a disobedience does not differ according to the assumption and reckoning of its doer; rather, that may even confirm its greatness, since they were ignorant that it was great.

The third: it is obligatory upon the accountable person, regarding every prohibited act, to regard greatly the undertaking of it, since he cannot be sure that it is not among the major sins. It has been said: there is no minor sin with persistence, and no major sin with seeking forgiveness.

The fifth category: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did you not say, "It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You! This is a tremendous slander"?﴾

This is from the category of good manners (adab). That is, "Why did you not, when you heard it, say, 'It is not for us to speak of this'?" The reasons why it was obligatory for them to refrain from it are as follows:

First: The factor that makes them abstain from this act is present, namely intellect and religion, and nothing opposes it. So the presumption that they abstained from sin must be stronger than the presumption that they committed it. If He had reported that they had committed the sin, He would have preferred the weaker over the stronger, which is impermissible.

Second: It involves harming the Messenger, and that is a cause of being cursed, as He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger, Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter﴾ [al-Ahzab: 57].

Third: It causes harm to ʿAʾishah, to her parents, and to those connected with them, without any known cause or any known offence committed by them, and that is forbidden.

Fourth: It is an act that may cause harm while one can do without it, and reason requires keeping away from it. For the slanderer, if he is truthful, does not deserve reward for his truthfulness; rather he deserves punishment, because he has spread indecency. And if he is lying, he deserves a great punishment. Clear reason requires avoiding such things.

Fifth: It is a squandering of time on what has no benefit. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Part of the goodness of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him."

Sixth: Displaying people's good qualities and concealing their faults is a way of adopting the character of Allah, exalted is He. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Adopt the character of Allah."

These considerations make it obligatory for the intelligent person, when he hears a slander, to remain silent about it and to strive to avoid falling into it. If it is asked: How was it permissible to separate "lawla" (why not) from "qultum" (you said) by the adverbial phrase? We answer: The benefit in it is that it was obligatory for them to refrain from speaking of the lie from the very first moment they heard of the falsehood.

As for His saying: ﴿Glory be to You! This is a tremendous slander﴾, there are two questions concerning it.

The first question: How is "Subhanaka" (Glory be to You) appropriate in this context? The answer has several aspects:

The first: It is meant to express amazement at the magnitude of the matter. It is used in the sense of amazement because one glorifies Allah upon seeing something wondrous in His creation. Then its use became widespread until it was applied to anything one marvels at.

The second: It is meant to declare Allah exalted above the wife of His Prophet being an adulteress.

The third: He is exalted above being pleased with the oppression of these slanderous people.

The fourth: He is exalted above not punishing these wicked slanderers.

The second question: Why were they obligated to say "This is a tremendous slander" when they did not know with certainty that it was a lie? The answer has two aspects:

The first: They were able to know that it was a slander, because the Messenger's wife cannot be an adulteress.

The second: Since they affirmed that they had not entertained it in their hearts, their report of that affirmation would be a lie. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1].

[Page 158]

This is from the category of deterrents. The meaning is: God admonishes you with these admonitions, by which you recognize the gravity of this sin, and that in it are the prescribed punishment (hadd) and the chastisement in this world and the torment in the Hereafter, so that you do not return to the like of this act ever. "Ever" means for as long as they are alive and legally accountable. Included in this is whoever spoke and whoever heard and did not denounce it, because their state is equal in that both committed what is not permitted, although the one who initiated it bears the greater sin. Thus He made clear that the purpose of what He taught them through this method is that they not return to the like of what had previously occurred from them. Here there are several questions.

**First question:** The Mu'tazilah (the rationalist school) cited His words, ﴿if you are believers﴾, as evidence that abstaining from slander is part of faith, and that committing slander does not leave faith intact with it, because what is conditioned on a condition is non-existent when the condition is non-existent. The answer: this is opposed by His words, ﴿Indeed, those who brought the slander are a group among you﴾, meaning among you, O believers. This indicates that slander does not necessitate exit from faith. Since the contradiction is established, we interpret this verse as an incitement toward admonition and restraint.

**Second question:** The Mu'tazilah said: this verse indicates that He, exalted is He, intended from all whom He admonished that they avoid the like of that in the future, even if among them there are those who do not obey. From this aspect it indicates that He wills obedience from all of them even if they disobey, because His words, ﴿God admonishes you that you return﴾, mean "so that you do not return to the like of it," and that is the indication of will. The answer to this has been given repeatedly before.

**Third question:** Is it permissible to call God an admonisher (wa'iz) on the basis of His words, ﴿God admonishes you﴾? The more apparent view is that it is not permissible, just as it is not permissible to call Him a teacher (mu'allim) on the basis of His words, ﴿The Most Merciful, taught the Qur'an﴾ [al-Rahman: 1–2].

As for His words, ﴿And God makes the verses clear to you, and God is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾: the meaning of "verses" here is that by which a person knows what he should hold fast to. Then He made clear that, because He is All-Knowing and All-Wise, He influences by what He must make clear, and He must be obeyed for that reason. This is because one who is not knowing, his commands must not be accepted, since he may command what is not fitting. Also, if a legally accountable person obeys him, he may not know that he has obeyed him, and then there would be no benefit in obedience. As for one who is knowing but not wise, he may command him with what is not fitting; if the accountable person obeys him, he may torment the obedient or reward the disobedient, and then there would be no benefit in obedience. But when He is All-Knowing and All-Wise, He commands only what is fitting and does not neglect the recompense of those who deserve it. Therefore He mentioned these two attributes and singled them out for mention. Here there are questions:

**The first:** The Wise is the one who does not bring about what is not fitting, and he is only so if he knows the ugliness of what is ugly and knows that he is free of it. Thus the All-Knowing is included within the Wise, and so mentioning the Wise would suffice without it. This is according to the Mu'tazilah's view. As for the view of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah (the Sunni majority), wisdom is knowledge alone, so mentioning "All-Knowing, All-Wise" would be pure repetition. The answer: it is taken as emphasis.

**The second question:** The Mu'tazilah said: the verse indicates that it is necessary to accept God's exposition only because He is knowing and wise, and the Wise is the one who does not commit ugly acts. So the verse indicates that if He were the creator of ugly acts, it would not be permissible to rely upon His promise and His threat. The answer: the Wise, according to us, is the All-Knowing, and reliance upon His speech is permissible because He knows all things, since the ignorant person's speech is not relied upon at all.

**The third question:** The Mu'tazilah said: His words, ﴿God makes clear to you﴾, meaning "for your sake," indicate that His acts are caused by purposes. Also, His words, ﴿to you﴾, cannot be taken in their apparent sense, because the purpose is not their essences themselves, but the attainment of their benefit, obedience, and faith. From this it follows that He wills faith from all. The answer: what is meant is that He, glory be to Him, did to them what, if another had done it, would have been a purpose.

**Category seven: His saying, exalted is He:** ﴿Indeed, those who love that immorality should spread among those who have believed will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And Allah knows, while you do not know.﴾

Know that when He, glory be to Him, explained what is incumbent upon the people of the slander (*ahl al-ifk*) and upon those who heard it from them, and the religious etiquette they should adhere to, He followed it with His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who love that immorality should spread﴾, so that it would be known that whoever loves that has shared in this blame just as whoever committed it has, and whoever did not denounce it has too. It also shows that just as the people of the slander deserve punishment for what they openly displayed, they likewise deserve punishment for what they concealed of loving the spread of immorality among the believers. This indicates that it is obligatory to keep the heart free from harm toward the believers, just as it is obligatory to restrain the limbs and speech from what harms them. Here are some issues:

**First issue:** *al-isha'ah* (spreading) means dissemination. It is said of a property, "a *sahm shā'i'*" (a share held in common) when it belongs to everyone and is not divided off. And "the report spread" (*shā'a al-ḥadīth*) when it became known among the common people.

**Second issue:** There is no doubt that the apparent meaning of His saying ﴿Indeed, those who love﴾ indicates generality, and that it encompasses everyone who has this attribute. There is also no doubt that this verse was revealed concerning the slander against ʿĀʾishah, but the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specific cause. Therefore it is necessary to apply it to its apparent generality. Among what shows that it is not permissible to restrict it to the slanderers of ʿĀʾishah is His saying ﴿among those who have believed﴾, for it is a plural form. Had He intended ʿĀʾishah alone, that would not have been permissible. Those who restricted it to the slanderers of ʿĀʾishah include some who understood it as referring to ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy, because he was the one who strove to spread the immorality. They said the meaning of the verse is: ﴿Indeed, those who love﴾, and the intended one is ʿAbdullāh, ﴿that immorality should spread﴾, that is, fornication, ﴿among those who have believed﴾, that is, among ʿĀʾishah and Ṣafwān.

**Third issue:** It is narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Indeed, I know of people who strike their chests with a blow that the people of the Fire will hear. They are the *hammāzūn* and *lammāzūn* (backbiters and slanderers), who seek out the faults of the Muslims, expose their concealed matters, and spread among them immoral things that are not in them." And from him, peace be upon him: "No believing servant conceals the fault of another believing servant except that Allah conceals his fault on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever relieves a Muslim of his transaction (*aqāla muslimān ṣafqatah*), Allah will relieve his stumble on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever conceals another's faults, Allah will conceal his faults on the Day of Resurrection." And from him, peace be upon him: "The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe, and the emigrant (*muhājir*) is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden." 

And from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, from him, peace be upon him, who said: "Whoever would like to be drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise, let his death come to him while he testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and let him love that people be treated by him as he loves to be treated." And from Anas, who said: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "A servant does not believe until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself of good."

**Fourth issue:** They differed concerning the punishment of this world. Some said it is the establishment of the *ḥadd* (prescribed punishment) upon them. Others said it is the *ḥadd* and the curse and enmity from Allah and the believers. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy, Ḥassān, and Mistaḥ. Ṣafwān lay in wait for Ḥassān and struck him a blow with the sword, which blinded his sight. Al-Ḥasan said: it refers to the hypocrites, because they intended to grieve the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and whoever intends to grieve the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is a disbeliever. Their punishment in this world is what they were toiling in and spending on, to fight their allies alongside their enemies.

Abū Muslim said: "Those who love" are the hypocrites, who love that. So Allah threatened them with punishment in this world at the hand of the Messenger ﷺ through striving against them, according to His saying: ﴿Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 73]. The closest view is that what is meant by this punishment is what they deserved by their slander, namely the *ḥadd*, the curse, and blame. As for the punishment of the Hereafter, there is no doubt that there is punishment in the grave, and in the Resurrection the punishment of the Fire.

As for His saying ﴿And Allah knows, while you do not know﴾, it is well placed in this context, because the love of the heart is hidden, and we do not know it except through signs, whereas Allah, glory be to Him, nothing is hidden from Him. Thus this mention is a utmost deterrent, for whoever loves the spread of immorality, even if he exaggerates in concealing that love, knows that Allah knows it about him, and that His knowledge of what he concealed is like His knowledge of what he displayed, and he knows the measure of the recompense for it.

**Fifth issue:** The verse indicates that resolving upon a great sin is great, and that intending wrongdoing is wrongdoing, since He attached the threat to the love of spreading immorality.

**Sixth issue:** Al-Jubbāʾī said: The verse indicates that every slanderer who does not repent of his slander has no reward, insofar as he deserved this everlasting punishment, and that prevents him from deserving its opposite, which is reward. From this aspect, it indicates what we say regarding the threat. Know that its conclusion returns to the issue of *al-muḥābaṭah* (the nullification of good deeds by sin), and the discussion of it has already passed.

**Seventh issue:** The Muʿtazilah said: Allah, exalted is He, emphasized the blame of whoever loves the spread of immorality. So if Allah were the Creator of the actions of the servants, then no one would be the spreader of immorality except Him, and therefore no one should deserve blame for spreading immorality except Him, because He is the One who performed that spreading, and no one else performed any of it. The discussion of this has also already passed.

**Eighth issue:** Abū Ḥanīfah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: A woman afflicted with wickedness (*al-muṣābah bil-fujūr*) is not to be interrogated, because interrogating her is spreading immorality, and that is forbidden.

The eighth category: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Kind and Merciful﴾

There are several aspects to it:

The first: its response (jawab) is omitted, as if He had said: "You would have been destroyed," or "Allah would have punished you and uprooted you, but He is Kind (ra'uf) and Merciful." Ibn 'Abbas said: the address is to Hassan, Mistah and Hamnah. It is also permissible that the address be general.

The second: its response is in His saying: ﴿Not one of you would ever have been pure﴾ [al-Nur: 21].

The third: its response is: "the immorality would have spread, and the harm would have grown great." This is the view of Abu Muslim. The closer view is that its response is omitted, because His saying after ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been pure﴾ is like something detached from the first, so it is not necessary that it be the response to the first, especially since another statement has come between the two statements. The meaning is that, were it not for His favour by which He let you remain, granted you respite, and enabled you to make amends, you would have perished; but, out of His compassion, He does not leave what is better for the servant even if the servant has harmed himself.

Category Nine: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not follow the footsteps of Satan. And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan — indeed, he enjoins immorality and wrongdoing. And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been pure. But Allah purifies whom He wills, and Allah is Hearing, Knowing.﴾

It has been recited as "khuṭuwāt" (خُطُواتِ) with a damma on the ṭā' and with a sukūn on it. Khuṭuwāt is the plural of khuṭwah (خَطْوَة), which derives from khaṭā al-rajul yakhṭū khaṭwan (the man stepped, taking a stride). When you want the singular, you say khaṭwah with a fatḥah on the first letter, and the plural has its first letter either fatḥah or ḍammah. What is meant by it is the conduct and the way. The meaning is: do not follow the traces of Satan, and do not take his paths in listening to the slander, accepting it, and spreading immorality among those who have believed. Although Allah, exalted is He, singled out the believers with this, it is a prohibition for all the responsible persons, and this is His saying: ﴿And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan — indeed, he enjoins immorality and wrongdoing﴾. It is known that all the responsible persons are forbidden from that.

We have said that He, exalted is He, singled out the believers with this, because He threatened them for following His footsteps with His saying: ﴿And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan﴾, and the apparent meaning of that is that they had not followed him. Had the intended meaning been the disbelievers, they would have followed him. So it is as if He, glorified is He, when He had made clear the threat upon the people of the slander, also disciplined the believers, by singling them out for mention so that they would be strict in abandoning disobedience, lest their condition become like the condition of the people of slander and immorality. Al-fāḥishah is that whose ugliness is excessive, and al-munkar is that which souls disapprove of, so they recoil from it and do not find it acceptable.

As for His saying: ﴿And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been pure﴾, Yaʿqūb and Ibn Muḥayṣin recited mā zakkā with shaddah. Know that the zakiyy (pure one) is one who has reached in obedience to Allah the level of contentment, and from it one says zakā al-zarʿu (the crop grew pure). When the believer reaches in righteousness in the religion the point that Allah, exalted is He, is pleased with, he is called zakiyy. One does not say zakiyy unless he has been found pure, just as one does not say of one who abandoned guidance that Allah guided him absolutely; rather one says "Allah guided him, but he did not become guided." Our companions argued in the question of the createdness (of the Qur'an) with His saying: ﴿But Allah purifies whom He wills﴾, and they said: purification is like blackening and reddening; just as blackening is the production of blackness, so purification is the production of purity in the locus. The Muʿtazilah said there are two interpretations here: the first: taking purification to mean the performance of kindnesses (alṭāf). The second: taking it to mean the judgment that the servant is pure. Our companions said: both interpretations are contrary to the apparent meaning. Then we establish the rational proof for the invalidity of both as well. As for the first interpretation, several points refute it:

The first of them: does the performance of kindness (luṭf) incline the motive or not incline it? If it does not incline it at all, there is no connection to it, so it is not a kindness. If it inclines it, then we say: the inclining must reach the degree of necessity, for with that degree of inclination, the act either becomes impossible at that point, or possible, or necessary. If it becomes impossible, it is a preventer, not a motive. If it is possible that it occurs and that it does not occur, then whatever is possible does not entail, from supposing its occurrence, something impossible. So let it be supposed at one time occurring and at another not occurring. The distinction of the time of occurrence from the time of non-occurrence either depends on the addition of a further condition to it, or does not depend on it. If it depends on it, the inclining factor is the whole that results after the addition of this condition, so what resulted first is not the inclining factor. If it does not depend on it, then the specification of one of the two times with occurrence and the other with non-occurrence is a preponderance of the possible without a preponderant, and that is impossible. As for the claim that the kindness is an inclining necessitating factor, then the agent of the kindness is the agent of what the kindness is applied to, and so Allah, exalted is He, would be the agent of the servant's act.

The second: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But Allah purifies whom He wills﴾; He made purification contingent on will, while the performance of kindness is obligatory, and what is obligatory is not contingent on will.

The third: He made purification contingent on bounty and mercy, while the creation of kindnesses is obligatory, so it is not contingent on bounty and mercy.

As for the second interpretation, which is the judgment that he is pure: that is obligatory, because if no judgment were made of it, it would be a lie, and lying against Allah, exalted is He, is impossible. So how could it be permissible to make it contingent on will? Thus it is established that His saying: ﴿But Allah purifies whom He wills﴾ is an explicit text on this matter.

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is Hearing, Knowing﴾, the meaning is that He hears your statements in slander and your statements in establishing innocence, and He knows what is in your hearts of love for spreading immorality or of hatred for it. And when this is so, it is obligatory to guard against disobeying Him.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 24, verse 22 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Let not those of virtue and abundance among you swear not to give to the near of kin, the needy, and those who emigrate in the way of Allah. Let them pardon and overlook. Do you not wish that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾

Know that just as He disciplined the people of the slander (al-ifk) and those who heard their words, as we have mentioned, He likewise disciplined Abu Bakr when he swore that he would never spend on Mistah. The exegetes (al-mufassirun) said: "The verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr when he swore that he would not spend on Mistah, who was the son of Abu Bakr's maternal aunt. He had been an orphan in his care, and he used to spend on him and on his relatives. When the verse was revealed, Abu Bakr said to them, 'Get up, you are not of me and I am not of you, and let none of you enter upon me.' Mistah said, 'I implore you by Allah and by Islam, and I implore you by kinship and the ties of blood, not to make us need anyone else. At the beginning of the matter we had no sin.' He said to Mistah, 'If you do not speak, you have laughed.' He said, 'That was only out of amazement at the words of Hassan.' He did not accept his excuse, and said, 'Go away, O people, for Allah has not granted you any excuse or relief.' So they went out, not knowing where to go or in which direction to head on the earth. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent to him informing him that Allah, Exalted, had revealed to me a Book forbidding you to drive them out. Abu Bakr said 'Allahu akbar' and was delighted. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the verse to him, and when he reached His saying, ﴿Do you not wish that Allah should forgive you?﴾ he said, 'Yes, O Lord, I wish that I be forgiven,' and he said, 'I have indeed pardoned what happened.' Abu Bakr went to his house, sent to Mistah and his companions, and said, 'I accept what Allah has revealed, with head and eye. I did to you what I did only because Allah was angry with you. Now that He has pardoned you, welcome to you.' And he restored to him twice what he had given before that day."

Here there are several issues.

First issue: regarding His saying ﴿wa-la ya'tali﴾ (let not swear), there are two views.

The first, which is the well-known one, is that it is from ta'alla (to swear), with the form ifta'ala derived from al-ilyah (oath), and the meaning is "let not swear." Abu Muslim said this is weak for two reasons.

One: according to this interpretation, the apparent meaning of the verse would require prohibition of swearing to give, whereas they meant prohibition of swearing not to give. Thus this interpreter has placed negation in place of affirmation and made the forbidden thing commanded.

Two: it is rarely found in speech that ifta'altu is used in place of af'altu; it is found in place of fa''altu. Here "alaytu" from al-ilyah is ifta'altu. So one does not say af'altu, just as one does not say from alzamtu "iltazamtu," or from a'tayta "i'taytu."

Then he said regarding "ya'tali": its root is ya'talī, the yā' was dropped for jazm (apocopation), since it is a prohibition. It derives from your saying: "ma aluttu fulanan nusḥan" (I did not withhold sincere advice from so-and-so), "wa lam aal fi amri juhdan" (I did not fall short in my affair with effort), meaning I did not fall short. So: "wa la ya'al" and "wa la ya'tali," meaning one (does not fall short). The meaning is: do not fall short in doing good to them. It is common to find ifta'ala used in place of fa'ala: one says kasabtu and iktasabtu, sana'tu and i stana'tu, radītu and irtaḍaytu. This interpretation is the correct one, not the first. This interpretation is also reported from Abu 'Ubaydah.

Al-Zajjaj answered the first question: in oaths, the verb is not often elided. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And do not make Allah the target of your oaths, that you should be righteous﴾ (2:224), meaning "that you should not be righteous." Imru' al-Qays said:

"I said, 'By Allah's oath, I will not leave sitting, even if they cut off my head and my limbs to you.'"

meaning "I will not leave."

As for the second question, they answered that all the exegetes who preceded Abu Muslim interpreted the word as oath, and the statement of each one of them is evidence in the language, so how could all be wrong? This is supported by al-Hasan's reading: ﴿wa-la yatalla﴾.

Second issue: the exegetes agreed that by His saying ﴿those of virtue (ulu al-fadl)﴾ is meant Abu Bakr. This verse indicates that he, may Allah be pleased with him, was the most excellent of people after the Messenger (ﷺ), because the virtue mentioned in this verse is either worldly or religious. The first is invalid, because He mentioned it in a context of praise for him, and praise from Allah with regard to worldly matters is not permissible. Also, if it were so, His saying ﴿and abundance (al-sa'ah)﴾ would be a repetition. So it is necessarily the religious virtue that is meant. If anyone else were equal to him in rank in religion, he would not be the possessor of virtue, because an equal is not superior. When Allah established for him virtue absolutely, not restricted to one person over another, it is necessary that he be the most excellent of creation, with the exception of the Messenger (ﷺ), since the rule has been set aside regarding the Messenger (ﷺ) and remains in force regarding others.

If it is said: "We deny the consensus of the exegetes that this verse is specific to Abu Bakr," we reply: everyone who has studied the books of tafsir and hadith knows that the specificity of this verse to Abu Bakr reaches the level of tawatur (mass transmission). If it were permissible to deny it, it would be permissible to deny every mass-transmitted report.

Furthermore, this verse indicates that its meaning is the most excellent of people, and the community has agreed that the most excellent is either Abu Bakr or 'Ali. So when we show that 'Ali is not meant, the verse is established for Abu Bakr. We say that it is not 'Ali for two reasons:

One: what precedes this verse and what follows it relates to the daughter of Abu Bakr, so mentioning 'Ali in between would be incongruous.

Two: He, Exalted, described him as one of the people of abundance (ulu al-sa'ah), and 'Ali was not among the people of worldly abundance at that time. Thus it is established definitively that Abu Bakr is meant.

Know that Allah, Exalted, described Abu Bakr in this verse with amazing attributes, indicating the elevation of his station in religion:

First: He, glory be to Him, referred to him with the plural form, and when one is referred to with the plural form, it indicates the elevation of his station, as in His saying, Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We sent down the Reminder﴾ (15:9), and ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾ (108:1). Consider the person whom Allah, glory be to Him, referred to, with his majesty, by the plural form: how elevated must his station be.

Second: He described him as possessing virtue absolutely, without restricting it to one person over another. Virtue includes bestowing favour, and this indicates that, just as he, may Allah be pleased with him, was virtuous absolutely, he was also one who conferred virtue absolutely.

Third: bestowing (al-ifdal) is giving what is appropriate without return. One who gives a knife to someone who will kill himself is not called virtuous, because he gave what was not appropriate. One who gives in order to gain from it a return, whether material, praise, or commendation, is a seeker of gain. Allah, Exalted, has described him with this, saying: ﴿And the most righteous will be spared it, who gives his wealth to purify himself, and for whom no one has a favour to be repaid, except seeking the countenance of his Lord, the Most High﴾ (92:17–20). And He said regarding 'Ali: ﴿We feed you only for the sake of Allah; we do not want from you reward or thanks. Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day austere and distressing﴾ (76:9–10). So 'Ali gave out of fear of punishment, whereas Abu Bakr gave only for the countenance of his Lord, the Most High. Thus Abu Bakr's rank is higher, and his giving in bestowing was more complete and perfect.

Fourth: He said: ﴿those of virtue among you (ulu al-fadl minkum)﴾. The particle "min" here is for specification (li'l-tamyiz). It is as if He, glory be to Him, distinguished him from all the believers by the attribute of being possessors of virtue. The attribute by which distinction occurs is impossible to be found in others, otherwise it would not be distinctive of him in particular. This indicates that this attribute is specific to him and not to others, absolutely.

Fifth: it is possible to interpret virtue (al-fadl) as obedience to Allah, Exalted, and service to Him, and His saying ﴿and abundance (al-sa'ah)﴾ as beneficence toward the Muslims. It is as if he combined veneration of the command of Allah, Exalted, and compassion toward the creatures of Allah. These two are among the highest ranks of the truthful (al-siddiqin), and whoever is like this, Allah is with him, according to His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾ (16:128). And because of his characterization by these two attributes, He said to him: ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾ (9:40).

Sixth: a person is described as possessing abundance (al-sa'ah) only if he is generous and liberal. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The best of people is the one who benefits people." This indicates that he was the best of people in this respect. And he, may Allah be pleased with him, was generous and liberal in everything. Among his generosity: when he embraced Islam at the beginning of the day, he brought 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, Talhah, al-Zubayr, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and 'Uthman ibn Maz'un to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) after they had embraced Islam at his hand. His generosity lay in teaching, guiding to the religion, and giving of worldly goods, as is well known. So he deserves to be described as one of the people of abundance. Furthermore, suppose people differed as to whether his Islam preceded that of 'Ali or came after it, yet they agreed that 'Ali, when he embraced Islam, did not occupy himself with calling people to the religion of Muhammad (ﷺ), whereas Abu Bakr occupied himself with calling people. So Abu Bakr was the first of people to occupy himself with calling to the religion of Muhammad. There is no doubt that the highest rank in religion is this rank. Therefore it is necessary that the most excellent of people after the Messenger (ﷺ) be Abu Bakr from this aspect. Also, he (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever establishes a good sunnah, he will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts upon it until the Day of Resurrection." So Abu Bakr must have a reward like that of everyone who calls to Allah, and this indicates his excellence from this aspect as well.

Seventh: injustice from close relatives is more severe. The poet said:

"The injustice of close kin is more painful
upon a man than the striking of a keen Indian sword."

Also, when a person does good to another and that other repays him with harm, it is more grievous to him than when the harm comes from a stranger. Both aspects were combined in the case of Mistah. Then he harmed Abu Bakr with this kind of harm, which is the greatest kind of harm. Consider the extent of that injury in Abu Bakr's heart. Then He, glory be to Him, commanded him not to cut off his kindness from him, and to return with him to what he had been upon of goodness. This is among the greatest kinds of striving (mujahadat). There is no doubt that this is harder than fighting the disbelievers, because this is striving against the self, whereas that is striving against the disbeliever, and striving against the self is more difficult. For this reason the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "We have returned from the lesser jihad to the greater jihad."

Eighth: when Allah, Exalted, commanded Abu Bakr with this, He named him "those of virtue" and "those of abundance," as if He, glory be to Him, were saying: you are more excellent than to repay his harm with anything, and you are too broad of heart to attach any weight to worldly things. So it is not fitting for your virtue and breadth of heart to cut off your kindness from him because of what came from him of harm. It is well known that such an address indicates the utmost excellence and elevation in religion.

Ninth: the definite article (al-alif wa-l-lam) indicates generality. The alif and lam in "al-fadl" and "al-sa'ah" indicate that all virtue and all abundance belong to Abu Bakr, just as one says, "So-and-so is the world (al-'alam)," meaning he has reached such virtue that he has become as if he were the whole world, and all else is as nothing. This too is a great merit.

Tenth: His saying: ﴿And let them pardon and overlook﴾. There are several aspects to this:

Among them: pardon is the companion of piety, and whoever is stronger in pardon is stronger in piety, and whoever is so is more excellent, according to His saying: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ (49:13).

Among them: pardon and piety are mutually connected, and for this reason they were combined in him. As for piety, it is according to His saying: ﴿And the most righteous will be spared it﴾ (92:17). As for pardon, it is according to His saying: ﴿And let them pardon and overlook﴾.

Eleventh: He, glory be to Him, said to Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So pardon them and overlook﴾ (5:13). And He said regarding Abu Bakr: ﴿And let them pardon and overlook﴾. From this aspect it indicates that Abu Bakr was the second of two to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in all the moral qualities, even in pardon and overlooking.

Twelfth among them: His saying, ﴿Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?﴾ He mentioned Himself with the plural pronoun as a form of glorification. Also, He made His forgiveness of Abu Bakr conditional on his pardoning and overlooking (the offence), so once the condition was fulfilled, the consequence was bound to follow. Then His saying, ﴿that Allah should forgive you﴾, is in the imperfect (future) form, and it is not restricted to any particular matter. The verse therefore indicates that God has forgiven him in the future of his life without restriction. In this respect, he is the second of two for the Messenger ﷺ in His saying, ﴿That Allah may forgive you your former and latter sins﴾ [al-Fath: 2]. It is also evidence for the validity of Abu Bakr's leadership (imamah), may Allah be pleased with him. For if his leadership had been contrary to the truth, he would not have been forgiven without restriction. And it is evidence for the validity of what the Messenger ﷺ stated in the report of the glad tidings to the Ten, that Abu Bakr is in Paradise.

Thirteenth among them: When He said, ﴿Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?﴾, He described Himself as Ghafur and Rahim. Ghafur is an intensive form denoting abundant forgiveness. Thus He glorified Abu Bakr by addressing him with the plural form that signifies honour, and He glorified Himself by describing Himself with the intensive form of forgiveness. When the Great One glorifies Himself and then glorifies His addressee, the glorification that proceeds from Him for that person's sake must be of the utmost degree. For this reason we say that when He said, ﴿Indeed We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾ [al-Kawthar: 1], the gift had to be great. Thus the verse indicates that Abu Bakr is also the second of two for the Messenger ﷺ in this virtue.

Fourteenth among them: When He described him as one of "those of grace and abundance" in praise, it must be said that he was free of disobedience, because one praised to this degree cannot be among the people of the Fire. Had he been disobedient, he would have been so, given His saying, ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him to a Fire, abiding therein﴾ [an-Nisa: 14]. Since it is established that he was free of sins, His saying, ﴿that Allah should forgive you﴾, cannot mean the forgiveness of a sin, because a sin that does not occur cannot be forgiven. And when it is established that the verse cannot be interpreted in that way, it must be interpreted in another way. So it is as if He, may He be exalted, said, and Allah knows best: "Do you not love that Allah should forgive you, for the sake of your honouring these slanderers who are sinners?" The meaning of the verse therefore returns to this: He said, "O Abu Bakr, if you accept these sinners, I too will accept them; and if you reject them, I too will reject them." It is as if He granted him the rank of intercession in this world. This is what came to our minds regarding this verse, and Allah knows best.

If it is said: this verse detracts from the virtue of Abu Bakr in another respect, because He forbade him from this oath, which indicates that a sin proceeded from him. We answer with several points:

First: The prohibition does not indicate that it occurred. Allah, exalted is He, said to Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ [al-Ahzab: 1], and this does not indicate that he, peace be upon him, obeyed them. Rather, the apparent reports indicate that this oath did proceed from him. But on this assumption, the verse does not indicate what you claim.

Second: Grant that the oath proceeded from him; why do you say it was a sin? Refraining from bestowing favour may well be good, especially toward one who has wronged one who did good to him, or toward one who would use it as a means to forbidden acts. It cannot be said: "If it were not a sin, Allah would not have forbidden it by His saying, ﴿And let not those of grace and abundance swear﴾." For we say that this prohibition is not a prohibition of reproof and prohibition, but a prohibition of abandoning the better course. It is as if He said to Abu Bakr: "What befits your virtue and the breadth of your resolve is that you not cut this off." So this is guidance toward the better course, not a prohibition from what is forbidden.

Third issue: They agreed that by His saying, ﴿the near of kin and the needy and the emigrants in the way of Allah﴾, what is meant is Mistah, for he was a relative of Abu Bakr, was among the needy, and was among the emigrants. They differed about the sin that he committed. Some said he slandered, as did Abdullah ibn Ubayy. The Messenger ﷺ inflicted the prescribed punishment (hadd) upon him, and he repented of it. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: he was one who abandoned rejecting the evil and displayed approval. Whichever of the two matters it was, it is a sin.

* * *

Fourth issue: Our scholars used this verse as evidence against the doctrine of muhabata (the nullification of good deeds by sin). They said: He described him, after he had committed the slander, as one of the emigrants in the way of Allah, and this is a description of praise. This indicates that the reward for his being an emigrant was not nullified by his committing slander.

Fifth issue: They agreed that Mistah was among the People of Badr (ahl Badr, the companions present at the battle of Badr). It is established by a sound report that the Messenger ﷺ said: "Perhaps Allah looked upon the People of Badr and said: 'Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you.'" How, then, could a major sin proceed from him after he had been of the People of Badr? The answer is: it is not permissible that what is meant is "Do whatever you wish" of the sins, so that He commands them or upholds them, because we know by necessity that the obligation (taklif) remained upon them. If we interpreted it that way, it would entail the removal of obligation from them. Moreover, if it were so, Mistah could not have been punished for what he did and cursed. Therefore it must be interpreted as one of two matters. The first: He, exalted is He, looked upon the People of Badr, knowing their repentance and return, and said: "Do whatever voluntary acts you wish, few or many, for I have forgiven you and granted you the lofty ranks in Paradise." The second: It is possible that what is meant is that they will die in obedience. It is as if He said: "I have forgiven you because I know that you will die in repentance and return." He mentioned their state at the time and meant their final outcome.

* * *

Sixth issue: Pardoning and overlooking the offender is good and recommended. It may even be obligatory, and even if this verse were the only evidence for it, it would suffice. Do you not see His saying, ﴿Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?﴾ [an-Nur: 22], where He made forgiveness conditional upon pardoning and overlooking. And from him, peace be upon him, (it is reported): "Whoever does not accept the excuse of one who makes amends, whether he is lying or truthful, will not come to my Pool on the Day of Resurrection." And from him, peace be upon him: "The best of the morals of the Muslims is pardon." And also from him: "On the Day of Resurrection a caller will call out: 'Let whoever has a reward with Allah stand up.' None will stand except the people of pardon." Then he recited, ﴿So whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with Allah﴾. And also from him, peace be upon him: "A servant will not be of great merit until he joins the one who severed ties with him, pardons the one who wronged him, and gives to the one who deprived him."

Seventh issue: This verse indicates that an oath to refrain from good is not permissible. It is permissible only if it is made a motive toward good, not a deterrent from it.

* * *

Eighth issue: The position of the majority of jurists is that whoever swears an oath and then sees something other than it as better, it is fitting for him to do what is better and then make expiation (kaffarah) for his oath. Some said that he should do what is better, and that is his expiation. The one who held this view argued from the verse and a report. As for the verse, Allah, exalted is He, commanded Abu Bakr to break the oath (hinth) and did not require an expiation of him. As for the report, it is what is transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Whoever swears an oath and then sees something other than it as better, let him do what is better, and that is his expiation." As for the evidence of the majority's position, there are several points:

First: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿But He will hold you accountable for the oaths you have sworn firmly﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 89], so its expiation, and His saying, ﴿That is the expiation of your oaths when you swear﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 89]. This is general, covering one who breaks an oath in good as well as in other matters.

Second: His saying, exalted is He, concerning Ayyub when he swore to beat his wife: ﴿And take in your hand a bundle and strike with it, and do not break your oath﴾ [Sad: 44]. We know that breaking the oath was better than keeping it, and Allah commanded him to strike her with something that would not cause harm. Had breaking it been its expiation, he would not have been commanded to strike her; rather he would have broken it without expiation.

Third: His saying, peace be upon him: "Whoever swears an oath and then sees something other than it as better, let him do what is better and let him make expiation for his oath." As for the answer to what he cited first, it is that Allah did not mention the matter of expiation in the story of Abu Bakr, neither negating nor affirming it, because its ruling was known from the other verses. As for the answer to what he cited second, His saying, peace be upon him: "Let him do what is better, and that is his expiation," its meaning is the expiation of the sin, not the expiation mentioned in the Book. That is because he was forbidden from breaking oaths, so here he was commanded to break it and to repent, and he was informed that this would expiate the sin he committed by swearing.

* * *

Ninth issue: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad related from A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "I was favoured over the wives of the Prophet ﷺ with ten qualities: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married me while I was a virgin, unlike any other of his wives; my parents were both emigrants; Jibril, peace be upon him, brought my image in a silk cloth and commanded him to marry me; I used to bathe with him from one vessel; Jibril, peace be upon him, would descend to him with revelation while I was with him under one blanket; he married me in Shawwal and consummated the marriage with me in that month; he died while his head was between my chest and my neck; Allah, exalted is He, sent down my innocence from the heavens; and he was buried in my house. None of these was shared with me by any other." 

Some said: Allah cleared four by four: He cleared Yusuf, peace be upon him, by the tongue of a witness, ﴿And a witness from among her people testified﴾; He cleared Musa, peace be upon him, from the claim of the Jews by the stone that carried off his garment; He cleared Maryam by making her child speak; and He cleared A'ishah by these great verses in His Book, which is inimitable and recited throughout time.

It is reported that when the death of A'ishah drew near, Ibn 'Abbas came asking permission to enter upon her. She said: "He is coming now, and he will praise me." Ibn al-Zubayr informed him, and he said: "I will not go back until you grant me permission." She granted him permission, and he entered. A'ishah said: "I seek refuge in Allah from the Fire." Ibn 'Abbas said: "O Mother of the Believers, what is it to you with the Fire, when Allah has protected you from it, and sent down your innocence, which is recited in the mosques, and purified you?" He said: ﴿The good women are for the good men, and the good men for the good women﴾ [an-Nur: 26]. "You were the most beloved of the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to him, and he loved none but the good. And because of you the tayammum was revealed, so He said: ﴿Then seek clean earth﴾ [an-Nisa: 43]." 

It is also reported that A'ishah and Zaynab boasted to one another. Zaynab said: "I am the one whose marriage my Lord sent down." A'ishah said: "I am the one whom my Lord cleared when Ibn al-Mu'attal carried me on the mount." Zaynab said to her: "What did you say when you mounted it?" She said: "I said: 'Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.'" Zaynab said: "You said the word of the believers."

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 24, verses 23–25:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and for them is a great punishment.﴾ ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do.﴾ ﴿On that Day Allah will pay them their due reward in full, and they will know that Allah is the Manifest Truth.﴾

In this there are two issues:

The first issue: Scholars differ regarding His words, ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary women﴾, whether the intended meaning is everyone who has this description, or whether it is specific. As for the jurists of legal theory (usuliyyun), they said: the expression is general, and there is no barrier to applying it to its apparent meaning, so it must be taken in its general sense, and it therefore includes the slanderers of ʿĀʾisha and the slanderers of others. Some people disagreed with this and mentioned several views:

The first: that the intended meaning is the slanderers of ʿĀʾisha. ʿĀʾisha said: "I was accused while I was unwary, and I only learned of it later. Then while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with me, Allah revealed to him, and he said: 'Rejoice, O ʿĀʾisha,' and he recited: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women﴾."

The second: that the intended meaning is all the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that because of their nobility they were singled out, so that whoever slanders them falls under this threat. Those who held this view argued with several points:

The first: the repentance of the slanderer of other chaste women is accepted, according to His words at the beginning of the surah: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾ up to His words: ﴿And those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ ﴿except those who repent﴾ [An-Nur: 4–5]. But the slanderer in this verse, his repentance is not accepted, because He, exalted is He, said: ﴿they are cursed in this world and the Hereafter﴾ and did not mention an exception. Also, this is the description of the hypocrites in His words: ﴿cursed wherever they are found﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 61].

The second: the slanderer of other chaste women does not commit kufr, whereas the slanderer in this verse does commit kufr, because of His words: ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will testify against them﴾, and this is the description of disbelievers and hypocrites, as in His words: ﴿And on the Day when the enemies of Allah are gathered to the Fire﴾ [Fussilat: 19] and the three verses that follow.

The third: He said: ﴿and for them is a great punishment﴾, and a great punishment is the punishment of kufr. This indicates that the punishment of this slanderer is the punishment of kufr, and the punishment for his slandering of other chaste women is not the punishment of kufr.

The fourth: It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him both, that he was in Basra on the Day of ʿArafa, and he was being asked about the interpretation of the Qur'an. He was asked about the interpretation of this verse, and he said: "Whoever commits a sin and then repents, his repentance is accepted, except for whoever engaged in the matter of ʿĀʾisha." The jurists of legal theory answered him: the threat mentioned in this verse must be conditional upon not repenting, because a sin, whether it is kufr or fisq, once repentance occurs from it, becomes forgiven, and so the question is resolved. Some people mentioned another view, namely that this verse was revealed concerning the polytheists of Mecca at the time when there was a treaty between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Whenever a woman went out to Medina as a emigrant, the polytheists of Mecca would slander her and say: "She only went out to commit fornication." So this verse was revealed concerning them. The first view is the correct one.

The second issue: Allah, exalted is He, mentioned three things concerning those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women. The first: that they are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and this is a severe threat. Al-Jubba'i argued that the restriction by the curse is general to all slanderers, and whoever is cursed in this world is cursed in the Hereafter, and one who is cursed in the Hereafter is not among the people of Paradise. This is built upon the doctrine of mutual cancellation (muhabata), and its discussion has already passed. The second: His words: ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾, and its parallel is His words: ﴿And they will say to their skins: "Why did you testify against us?"﴾ [Fussilat: 21]. According to us, bodily structure is not a condition for life, so it is permissible for Allah, exalted is He, to create in an indivisible atom knowledge, power, and speech. According to the Mu'tazila, this is not permissible, so they necessarily mentioned two interpretations of this verse:

The first: that He, glorified is He, creates this speech in these limbs, and according to them the speaker is the doer of speech, so that testimony is in reality from Allah, exalted is He, except that He attributed it to the limbs figuratively.

The second: that He, glorified is He, reshapes these limbs contrary to what they are, and compels them to testify against the human being and inform about his deeds. Al-Qadi said: this is closer to the apparent meaning, because that indicates they perform the testimony. The third: His words, exalted is He: ﴿On that Day Allah will pay them their due reward in full﴾, and there is no doubt that the very "dīn" of theirs is not what is meant, because their dīn is their deed. Rather, what is meant is the recompense for their deeds, and dīn in the sense of recompense is used, as in the saying "As you judge, so you will be judged." It was also said that dīn here means reckoning, as in His words: ﴿That is the upright dīn﴾, meaning the correct reckoning. The meaning of His words ﴿al-ḥaqq﴾ (the due) is that what He pays them of recompense is the amount that is deserved, because it is the truth (ḥaqq), and whatever exceeds it is falsehood. It is also read ﴿al-ḥaqqa﴾ in the accusative as an attribute of dīn, which is recompense, and in the nominative as an attribute of Allah.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿and they will know that Allah is the Manifest Truth﴾, some people said that He, glorified is He, was named "the Truth" (al-Ḥaqq) because His worship is the truth, to the exclusion of the worship of others, or because He is the truth in what He commands, to the exclusion of others. The meaning of ﴿al-Mubin﴾ (the Manifest) supports what we have said, because the one who is right in what he addresses is the manifest one, insofar as he makes the correct clear by his speech, to the exclusion of others. Others said that al-Ḥaqq is among the names of Allah, exalted is He, and its meaning is the existent, because its opposite is falsehood, which is the non-existent. The meaning of al-Mubin is the one who makes manifest, and its meaning is that by His power the existence of possible things became manifest. So the meaning of His being True is that He is existent in Himself, and the meaning of His being Manifest is that He is the giver of existence to others.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 24, verses 23–25:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and for them is a great punishment.﴾ ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do.﴾ ﴿On that Day Allah will pay them their due reward in full, and they will know that Allah is the Manifest Truth.﴾

In this there are two issues:

The first issue: Scholars differ regarding His words, ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary women﴾, whether the intended meaning is everyone who has this description, or whether it is specific. As for the jurists of legal theory (usuliyyun), they said: the expression is general, and there is no barrier to applying it to its apparent meaning, so it must be taken in its general sense, and it therefore includes the slanderers of ʿĀʾisha and the slanderers of others. Some people disagreed with this and mentioned several views:

The first: that the intended meaning is the slanderers of ʿĀʾisha. ʿĀʾisha said: "I was accused while I was unwary, and I only learned of it later. Then while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with me, Allah revealed to him, and he said: 'Rejoice, O ʿĀʾisha,' and he recited: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women﴾."

The second: that the intended meaning is all the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that because of their nobility they were singled out, so that whoever slanders them falls under this threat. Those who held this view argued with several points:

The first: the repentance of the slanderer of other chaste women is accepted, according to His words at the beginning of the surah: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾ up to His words: ﴿And those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ ﴿except those who repent﴾ [An-Nur: 4–5]. But the slanderer in this verse, his repentance is not accepted, because He, exalted is He, said: ﴿they are cursed in this world and the Hereafter﴾ and did not mention an exception. Also, this is the description of the hypocrites in His words: ﴿cursed wherever they are found﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 61].

The second: the slanderer of other chaste women does not commit kufr, whereas the slanderer in this verse does commit kufr, because of His words: ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will testify against them﴾, and this is the description of disbelievers and hypocrites, as in His words: ﴿And on the Day when the enemies of Allah are gathered to the Fire﴾ [Fussilat: 19] and the three verses that follow.

The third: He said: ﴿and for them is a great punishment﴾, and a great punishment is the punishment of kufr. This indicates that the punishment of this slanderer is the punishment of kufr, and the punishment for his slandering of other chaste women is not the punishment of kufr.

The fourth: It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him both, that he was in Basra on the Day of ʿArafa, and he was being asked about the interpretation of the Qur'an. He was asked about the interpretation of this verse, and he said: "Whoever commits a sin and then repents, his repentance is accepted, except for whoever engaged in the matter of ʿĀʾisha." The jurists of legal theory answered him: the threat mentioned in this verse must be conditional upon not repenting, because a sin, whether it is kufr or fisq, once repentance occurs from it, becomes forgiven, and so the question is resolved. Some people mentioned another view, namely that this verse was revealed concerning the polytheists of Mecca at the time when there was a treaty between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Whenever a woman went out to Medina as a emigrant, the polytheists of Mecca would slander her and say: "She only went out to commit fornication." So this verse was revealed concerning them. The first view is the correct one.

The second issue: Allah, exalted is He, mentioned three things concerning those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women. The first: that they are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and this is a severe threat. Al-Jubba'i argued that the restriction by the curse is general to all slanderers, and whoever is cursed in this world is cursed in the Hereafter, and one who is cursed in the Hereafter is not among the people of Paradise. This is built upon the doctrine of mutual cancellation (muhabata), and its discussion has already passed. The second: His words: ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾, and its parallel is His words: ﴿And they will say to their skins: "Why did you testify against us?"﴾ [Fussilat: 21]. According to us, bodily structure is not a condition for life, so it is permissible for Allah, exalted is He, to create in an indivisible atom knowledge, power, and speech. According to the Mu'tazila, this is not permissible, so they necessarily mentioned two interpretations of this verse:

The first: that He, glorified is He, creates this speech in these limbs, and according to them the speaker is the doer of speech, so that testimony is in reality from Allah, exalted is He, except that He attributed it to the limbs figuratively.

The second: that He, glorified is He, reshapes these limbs contrary to what they are, and compels them to testify against the human being and inform about his deeds. Al-Qadi said: this is closer to the apparent meaning, because that indicates they perform the testimony. The third: His words, exalted is He: ﴿On that Day Allah will pay them their due reward in full﴾, and there is no doubt that the very "dīn" of theirs is not what is meant, because their dīn is their deed. Rather, what is meant is the recompense for their deeds, and dīn in the sense of recompense is used, as in the saying "As you judge, so you will be judged." It was also said that dīn here means reckoning, as in His words: ﴿That is the upright dīn﴾, meaning the correct reckoning. The meaning of His words ﴿al-ḥaqq﴾ (the due) is that what He pays them of recompense is the amount that is deserved, because it is the truth (ḥaqq), and whatever exceeds it is falsehood. It is also read ﴿al-ḥaqqa﴾ in the accusative as an attribute of dīn, which is recompense, and in the nominative as an attribute of Allah.
